articles.articleText: Toyota Kasım 2026 kampanyaları açıklandı! İşte indirimli modeller ve kredi kampanyaları Toyota'nın kasım ayı fiyat listesi belli oldu. Corolla 1 milyon 965 bin TL'den, Yaris Hybrid 2 milyon 100 bin TL'den başlayan kampanyalı fiyatlarla satışa sunuluyor. Hilux'ta 1 milyon TL'ye 6 ay sıfır faizli kredi, Land Cruiser Prado'da 500 bin TL takas desteği bulunuyor. Toyota'nın kasım ayı fiyatları belli oldu Toyota, Kasım 2026 döneminde geçerli güncel fiyatlarını ve kampanyalarını duyurdu. Markanın Corolla, Yaris Hybrid, C-HR Hybrid ve Hilux gibi modellerinde fiyat avantajları ve farklı kampanyalar öne çıkıyor. Corolla ve Yaris modellerinde kampanyalı fiyatlar Toyota'nın kasım ayı fiyat listesinde bazı modellerin kampanyalı satış fiyatları şöyle: Corolla Cross Hybrid ve Hilux fiyatları Toyota'nın diğer modellerinde açıklanan liste ve kampanyalı fiyatlar da belli oldu. Yaris Hybrid 2,1 milyon TL'den başlıyor Toyota Yaris Hybrid, kasım ayında 2 milyon 100 bin TL'den başlayan kampanyalı fiyatıyla satışa sunuluyor. Modelin tavsiye edilen liste fiyatı 2 milyon 546 bin 500 TL olarak açıklanırken kampanya, 2026 model yılı Yaris Hybrid için 1-30 Kasım 2026 tarihleri arasında geçerli. C-HR Hybrid için açıklanan 2 milyon 290 bin TL'lik kampanyalı fiyat ise ÖTV muafiyetli araç alımlarına özel olarak sunuluyor. Hilux alacaklara 1 milyon TL'ye sıfır faizli kredi Toyota Hilux için kasım ayında dikkat çeken kredi kampanyası bulunuyor. Tüzel müşterilere özel olarak 1 milyon TL kredi, 6 ay vade ve yüzde 0 faiz fırsatı sunuluyor. Kampanya bireysel müşteriler için geçerli değil. Yeni Hilux'un kampanyalı satış fiyatı ise 4 milyon 109 bin TL olarak açıklandı. Land Cruiser Prado'ya 500 bin TL takas desteği Toyota'nın büyük SUV modeli Land Cruiser Prado için kasım ayına özel 500 bin TL takas desteği sunuluyor. Farklı bir marka otomobile sahip olan müşteriler de mevcut araçlarını takasa vererek bu destekten yararlanabiliyor. Land Cruiser Prado'nun tavsiye edilen liste fiyatı 17 milyon 550 bin TL, kampanyalı fiyatı ise 12 milyon 490 bin TL olarak açıklandı.

articles.title: Sales of tinned food and bottled water jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch
articles.summary: Sales of essential goods such as hand sanitiser soar after the government called on households to be prepared for emergencies.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Sales of tinned food and bottled water jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch
articles.summaryTr: Sales of essential goods such as hand sanitiser soar after the government called on households to be prepared for emergencies.
articles.articleText: Sales of tinned food and bottled water jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch - Published Sales of essential goods such as bottled water and canned food soared in the 10 days following the launch of the government's "Be Ready" emergency preparedness campaign on 22 October, research indicates. Hand sanitiser sales were up 83%, sales of bottled water rose 67% and tinned and jarred goods climbed 37%, according to data from retail research firm Worldpanel by Numerator. The government's public awareness campaign encouraged people to stock up in case of disruption to essential services by severe weather or cyberattacks. However, Worldpanel said that while households were stockpiling essentials, they were not panic buying. The government campaign encouraged people to keep three days-worth of food and water in their homes. Wet wipes, a torch and cash were also recommended. After the campaign launch, the equivalent of an extra 400,000 people per day bought tinned meat, Worldpanel said, although the typical amount remained at 500g, which suggests a gradual stocking-up. "Shoppers clearly took notice of the 'Be Ready' campaign, but this wasn't panic buying, with less than a third of households buying bottled water in October," said Fraser McKevitt, head of retail and consumer insight at Worldpanel by Numerator. "Growth came from more people adding the recommended items on the government's checklist to their weekly shop, not from shoppers piling their trolleys high, which is very much in line with what the government wanted households to do," he said. Sales of tinned and jarred goods rose from £58.2m in the 10 days to 2 November 2025 to £79.5m over the same period in 2026. Bottled water sales jumped from £13.6m to £22.8m compared with a year earlier and hand sanitiser sales climbed from £497,000 to £908,000. Further evidence of stockpiling came from food firm Princes on Tuesday, which said demand for tinned tuna, meat and vegetables had risen following the government's campaign. Princes interim chief executive Giuseppe Mastrolia said the jump in demand "further reinforces the relevance of our core categories in providing affordable, nutritious and convenient food solutions". The "Be Ready" campaign warns that severe weather and cyber attacks could disrupt essential services, and British households need to make sure they have what they need - for example, bottled water, and long-life food that doesn't need to be kept in the fridge such as dried fruit and nuts. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said everyone should have "those supplies in the house to get you through those moments". Disaster recovery expert Lucy Easthope previously told the BBC that the UK was playing "massive catch up" to other European nations in terms of preparedness. These include France, Germany Denmark, Sweden, and Norway. A number of experts have been calling for the UK to put more emphasis on food security, with some arguing that the government itself should take responsibility for food stockpiling, rather than individual households. In October, a group of more than 180 experts signed an open letter, external to Burnham and first secretary of state Louise Haigh calling for local authorities to have a duty to prevent and respond to food supply emergencies. They pointed out that a government survey found that 29% of people in the UK could not afford to keep a few days worth of food in the house. Get in touch Have you been stockpiling? If so, what have you been buying? - Published23 October

articles.title: Thousands of 'off-grid' homes eligible for £250 to help with heating bills
articles.summary: Households dependent on either heating oil or LPG and are eligible for reduced council tax will benefit.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Thousands of 'off-grid' homes eligible for £250 to help with heating bills
articles.summaryTr: Households dependent on either heating oil or LPG and are eligible for reduced council tax will benefit.
articles.articleText: Thousands of 'off-grid' homes eligible for £250 to help with heating bills - Published Up to 20,000 homes using heating oil could get a £250 payment from the Welsh government to help with the rising cost of living. The government said £5m from a new £130m package will help "off grid" households who are dependent on either heating oil or LPG and are eligible for reduced council tax. The package includes the £100 household energy payment, with this extended to those eligible for council tax relief "irrespective of band". It also includes £7m support for bus travel and £8m for councils to help those "not captured by other schemes". It follows the UK government unveiling a £100 "household energy payment" for council taxpayers in bands A-D in England in October. Wales' Deputy First Minister Sioned Williams said supporting families with the cost of living was a "key priority". "We understand that this is a challenging time for many households across Wales," she said. "In total this represents an additional investment of £130m, providing immediate relief for households this winter. While we are taking firm action wherever we can, we need the UK Government to play its part". Five million pounds of the package will help towards "off-grid" fuel costs with a £250 payment available to households eligible for Council Tax Reduction based on their incomes and are dependent on either heating oil or LPG. An additional £8m will allow councils to extend the £100 payment to households "not captured" by other schemes and are facing financial hardship. While £7m is being made available to support bus operators with their high fuel costs and protect passengers from fares increases. The Welsh government said with winter approaching and the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, "the coming months will be a challenging time for many". "This package represents a significant investment in Welsh communities and reflects our determination to stand alongside households during challenging times," it added. The Welsh government had already said it would make the £100 energy payment to about one million households in Wales following Chancellor John Healey's UK Budget announcement in October. The chancellor said council taxpayers in bands A-D in England would get the payment and urged the Welsh government to follow his lead, with Wales' Finance Minister Elin Jones subsequently saying households in the same bands in Wales would also benefit. Healey announced an end to gas standing charges but did not address call to help those people, mainly in rural areas, who relied on either heating oil or LPG. Reform Wales leader Helen Jenner said: "At a time when families are struggling to pay their bills and public services are under pressure, Plaid Cymru continue to send millions of pounds abroad on overseas offices, disabled beekeeping schemes in Uganda and more than £60m on their Nation of Sanctuary scheme. "That money should be spent easing the cost of living and helping public services." Related topics More top stories - Published1 day ago

articles.articleText: Ali Koç'tan COP31'te kritik mesaj: Enerjide yeni dönem başlıyor - Koç Holding Yönetim Kurulu Başkan Vekili Ali Koç, COP31'in iklim hedeflerinin ötesinde enerji güvenliği ve bağımsızlığı açısından da önemli bir dönüm noktası olabileceğini söyledi. - Koç, jeopolitik krizlerin fosil yakıtlara bağımlılığın risklerini ortaya çıkardığını belirterek elektrifikasyon ve yenilenebilir enerjiye dikkat çekti. Koç Holding Yönetim Kurulu Başkan Vekili Ali Koç, CNBC-e canlı yayınında Emre Eser'in sorularını yanıtladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Koç, holdingin COP31'de küresel iş ortağı olarak yer almasını ve zirvenin Türkiye açısından yaratabileceği fırsatları değerlendirdi. Koç Topluluğu'nun 100'üncü yılında Türkiye'nin önemli bir iklim zirvesine ev sahipliği yapmasının kendileri için ayrı bir anlam taşıdığını belirten Ali Koç, enerji, otomotiv, rafineri ve marina faaliyetleri başta olmak üzere topluluğun farklı sektörlerdeki dönüşüm çalışmalarını uluslararası platformda anlatmak istediklerini söyledi. "Bu zirvenin en önemli söylemi aksiyon" COP31'in en önemli çıktısının somut adımlar olması gerektiğini vurgulayan Koç, iklim hedeflerinin yanı sıra enerji bağımsızlığı ve güvenliği konusunda da ilerleme sağlanmasını beklediğini ifade etti. Geçmiş iklim zirvelerinde taahhütlerin, hedeflerin ve takvimlerin öne çıktığını ancak bunların ne ölçüde hayata geçirildiğinin yeterince takip edilmediğini belirten Koç, bu kez uygulamaya odaklanılması gerektiğini söyledi. Koç, son dönemde yaşanan jeopolitik krizlerin ve doğal afetlerin enerji dönüşümünü daha acil hale getirdiğine dikkat çekti. "Fosil yakıtlara güven olmuyor" Ukrayna-Rusya savaşı ve Hürmüz Boğazı'nda yaşanan gelişmelerin enerji piyasalarındaki kırılganlığı ortaya koyduğunu belirten Ali Koç, fosil yakıt fiyatlarındaki dalgalanmaların ülkelerin ekonomilerini ve siyasi dengelerini etkilediğini söyledi. Koç, "Artık fosil yakıtlara güven olmuyor, fiyatlar çok oynuyor. Enerji piyasalarındaki inişler, çıkışlar ekonomileri etkiliyor. Artık bağımsız olmalıyız" dedi. Büyük ülkelerin içe dönük sanayileşme süreçlerine yöneldiğini belirten Koç, bu süreçte dayanıklılık ve enerji güvenliğinin öne çıktığını kaydetti. Enerji bağımsızlığında elektrifikasyon vurgusu Enerji bağımsızlığının sağlanmasında elektrifikasyonun önemli rol oynadığını ifade eden Koç, elektrik üretiminde yenilenebilir enerji kaynaklarının payının artırılması gerektiğini söyledi. Teknoloji, finansman ve liderlik başlıklarının COP31 gündeminde önemli yer tuttuğunu belirten Koç, tüm bu dönüşümün temelinde ekonomik rekabet gücünün bulunduğunu vurguladı. Koç, ekonomik çıkarlarla iklim hedeflerinin bugüne kadar hiç olmadığı kadar örtüştüğünü belirterek, ülkelerin artık yalnızca çevresel kaygılarla değil, enerji maliyetleri ve ekonomik çıkarları doğrultusunda da daha temiz ve güvenilir enerji kaynaklarına yöneldiğini ifade etti. Elektrifikasyon, ulaşım ve sanayi başta olmak üzere farklı alanlarda fosil yakıtların yerine elektrik kullanımının yaygınlaştırılmasını kapsıyor. Yenilenebilir kaynaklardan üretilen elektriğin kullanımının artması, ülkelerin enerji ithalatına bağımlılığını azaltma ve enerji arz güvenliğini güçlendirme hedefleri açısından önem taşıyor.

Geçmiş iklim zirvelerinde taahhütlerin, hedeflerin ve takvimlerin öne çıktığını ancak bunların ne ölçüde hayata geçirildiğinin yeterince takip edilmediğini belirten Koç, bu kez uygulamaya odaklanılması gerektiğini söyledi. Koç, son dönemde yaşanan jeopolitik krizlerin ve doğal afetlerin enerji dönüşümünü daha acil hale getirdiğine dikkat çekti. "Fosil yakıtlara güven olmuyor" Ukrayna-Rusya savaşı ve Hürmüz Boğazı'nda yaşanan gelişmelerin enerji piyasalarındaki kırılganlığı ortaya koyduğunu belirten Ali Koç, fosil yakıt fiyatlarındaki dalgalanmaların ülkelerin ekonomilerini ve siyasi dengelerini etkilediğini söyledi. Koç, "Artık fosil yakıtlara güven olmuyor, fiyatlar çok oynuyor. Enerji piyasalarındaki inişler, çıkışlar ekonomileri etkiliyor. Artık bağımsız olmalıyız" dedi. Büyük ülkelerin içe dönük sanayileşme süreçlerine yöneldiğini belirten Koç, bu süreçte dayanıklılık ve enerji güvenliğinin öne çıktığını kaydetti. Enerji bağımsızlığında elektrifikasyon vurgusu Enerji bağımsızlığının sağlanmasında elektrifikasyonun önemli rol oynadığını ifade eden Koç, elektrik üretiminde yenilenebilir enerji kaynaklarının payının artırılması gerektiğini söyledi. Teknoloji, finansman ve liderlik başlıklarının COP31 gündeminde önemli yer tuttuğunu belirten Koç, tüm bu dönüşümün temelinde ekonomik rekabet gücünün bulunduğunu vurguladı. Koç, ekonomik çıkarlarla iklim hedeflerinin bugüne kadar hiç olmadığı kadar örtüştüğünü belirterek, ülkelerin artık yalnızca çevresel kaygılarla değil, enerji maliyetleri ve ekonomik çıkarları doğrultusunda da daha temiz ve güvenilir enerji kaynaklarına yöneldiğini ifade etti. Elektrifikasyon, ulaşım ve sanayi başta olmak üzere farklı alanlarda fosil yakıtların yerine elektrik kullanımının yaygınlaştırılmasını kapsıyor. Yenilenebilir kaynaklardan üretilen elektriğin kullanımının artması, ülkelerin enerji ithalatına bağımlılığını azaltma ve enerji arz güvenliğini güçlendirme hedefleri açısından önem taşıyor.

articles.titleTr: Ali Koç'tan enerji yatırımı mesajı: 2026 çok zor oldu, 2027'de temkinli olmak lazım
articles.summaryTr: Ali Koç, enerji dönüşümü kapsamında Koç'un faaliyetlerini değer zincirinin farklı alanlarına genişletmeyi ve Türkiye dışında da enerji yatırımlarını değerlendirdiklerini söyledi. 2027 için likiditeye dikkat çeken Koç, zorunlu olmayan yatırımların ertelenmesini önerdi.
articles.articleText: Ali Koç'tan enerji yatırımı mesajı: 2026 çok zor oldu, 2027'de temkinli olmak lazım - Ali Koç, enerji dönüşümü kapsamında Koç'un faaliyetlerini değer zincirinin farklı alanlarına genişletmeyi ve Türkiye dışında da enerji yatırımlarını değerlendirdiklerini söyledi. 2027 için likiditeye dikkat çeken Koç, zorunlu olmayan yatırımların ertelenmesini önerdi. Koç Holding Yönetim Kurulu Başkan Vekili Ali Koç, Antalya'da düzenlenen COP31 Zirvesi'nde CNBC-e muhabiri Emre Eser'in sorularını yanıtladı. Enerji dönüşümü, elektrifikasyon, depolama ve yapay zeka yatırımlarına ilişkin değerlendirmelerde bulunan Koç, enerji sektöründeki faaliyet alanlarını genişletme ihtimalini gündemlerinde tuttuklarını ifade etti. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Koç, konuya ilişkin şunları söyledi: "Aslında arkadaşlarımızla konuşuyoruz. Biz bugüne kadar rafineriyi bir... rafineriyi bir tarafa koyuyorum. Dağıtımı bir tarafa koyuyorum Opet gibi. Biz elektriğin, enerjinin üretim tarafında olduk çoğunlukla. Ama öyle bir dünya geliyor ki, artık bu enerji dönüşümünde sadece üretimin değil, değer zincirin pek çok yerinde olmamız gerektiğini arkadaşlarla konuşuyoruz. Artı sadece Türkiye’de değil, Türkiye dışında da enerji ihtiyacı o kadar artıyor ki, orada da enerji yatırımına bakmamız lazım diye arkadaşlarla biz öyle bir, konuşuyoruz. Bakalım zaman neyi gösterecek." "2026 gerçekten çok zor oldu" 2027 yılına ilişkin beklentileri de değerlendiren Koç, 2026'nın hem kontrol dışındaki gelişmeler hem de kontrol edilebilir alanlardaki hatalar nedeniyle zor geçtiğini belirtti. Önümüzdeki dönemde seçim ekonomisine ilişkin tartışmaların da gündemde olabileceğine işaret eden Koç, küresel piyasalarda likiditenin öneminin artacağını dile getirdi. Yapay zeka şirketlerinin ilk kez kredi piyasalarına girdiğini ve yüksek miktarda borçlandığını belirten Koç, ABD hükümetinin bütçe açığının da finansman ihtiyacını artırdığına dikkati çekti. Koç, 2027 yılına ve önümüzdeki döneme ilişkin değerlendirmesinde şu ifadeleri kullandı: Her zaman biz temkinli, imserlikle başlarız yıla. Ama 2026 gerçekten çok zor oldu.. Önümüzdeki sene bir seçimlerden bahsediliyor. Seçim ekonomisi gerilimi, girilmez mi onu da bilmiyorum. Ama ileriye dönük olarak bence en önemlisi likidite, en azından önümüzdeki iki sene. Çünkü şöyle de bir durum var, bu yapay zeka firmaları ilk defa kredi piyasalarına girdiler ve inanılmaz derecede kredi çekiyorlar. Zaten piyasalar pahalıydı. Amerikan hükümetinin 2.2 trilyon açığı var. Onların da tahvil yayınlamaları gerekiyor piyasalara. Dolayısıyla kredi piyasaları daha da daralacak. Fiyatlar daha da artacak. Onun için bence ileriye dönük olarak en azından bir sene için biraz daha temkinli olmak lazım. Biraz daha likiditede kalmak lazım. Mecbur olmayan yatırımları bir nebze ertelemenin fayda olduğunu düşünüyorum. Ama bizim ülkemizin potansiyeli o kadar yüksek ki, bugünleri çok rahat geçeriz. Uzun vadede Türkiye’ye güvenen, inanan, yatırım yapan her zaman kazanmıştır. Ali Koç, Türkiye'nin uzun vadeli potansiyeline güvendiğini belirterek, Türkiye'ye yatırım yapanların uzun vadede kazançlı çıktığını ifade etti.

articles.title: Anthropic heads for lower than expected $1.3 trillion valuation in stock market debut
articles.summary: The AI company behind the Claude chatbot will offer its shares at between $70 and $78.

articles.titleTr: Anthropic heads for lower than expected $1.3 trillion valuation in stock market debut
articles.summaryTr: The AI company behind the Claude chatbot will offer its shares at between $70 and $78.
articles.articleText: Anthropic heads for lower than expected $1.3 trillion valuation in stock market debut - Published Anthropic, the AI company behind the Claude chatbot, could be valued at around $1.3 trillion (£1 trillion) when it lists its shares for sale on New York's Nasdaq stock exchange. The loss-making company says it will offer its shares for between $70 and $78 each and will raise up to $64bn when it floats this month. It would value Anthropic at between $1.1tn and $1.3tn which, although large, is below the $2tn some backers of the firm predicted in summer, according to the Financial Times. It is floating at a volatile time for AI firms. After last week's US midterm elections, the Nasdaq fell sharply on concerns a Democrat-led Congress could slow development of AI and the buildout of data centres. There are also wider fears over the billions of dollars being spent on AI and whether it will pay off. In its most recent results for the six months to the end of June, Anthropic's revenues jumped to $16.2bn from $1.1bn in the same period last year. However, its pre-tax loss jumped to $80.7bn from $12.9bn. Fiona Cincotta, a senior market analyst at City Index, said the $64bn Anthropic wants to raise is "fairly bullish" within "the volatility [and] concerns towards AI that we've seen in sort of particularly last week". She told Reuters: "It's showing that they are still sort of upbeat about the outlook as far as AI is concerned and that obviously that they think that the demand is going to be there." At $1.3tn, Anthropic's possible valuation is below SpaceX, Elon Musk's rocket, satellite and artificial intelligence company, which listed its shares in June and was valued at nearly $1.8tn. Anthropic is just five years old. It was co-founded in 2021 by brother and sister Dario and Daniela Amodei along with five others - all of whom worked at OpenAI, the rival AI giant behind ChatGPT. articles.title: US inflation higher than expected in October - here's what is happening with prices
articles.summary: Prices rose by 0.4% over the month, driven by increases in shelter, food and energy costs.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: US inflation higher than expected in October - here's what is happening with prices
articles.summaryTr: Prices rose by 0.4% over the month, driven by increases in shelter, food and energy costs.
articles.articleText: US inflation higher than expected in October - here's what is happening with prices - Published US inflation rose at a faster-than-expected pace in October, according to official figures. Prices rose by 0.4% in the month, which was lower than the 0.6% increase in September. However, analysts had expected prices to rise by 0.3%, and the higher-than-expected pace could add to arguments for the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at its next meeting in December. The new figures come a week after the midterm elections which were fought over cost-of-living pressures across the US. What is inflation? Inflation is the rate at which the price of products or services increases over time. For example, if a bottle of milk costs $1 but rises to $1.10 a year later, then annual inflation for bottled milk is 10%. Officials from the Bureau of Labor Statistics measure inflation through the consumer price index (CPI). It tracks the price changes of hundreds of day-to-day items including fresh food, gasoline and medical services to work out the overall level of inflation in the US economy. The bureau updates this so-called basket of goods over time as peoples' spending and lifestyle habits change. What causes inflation? There are several factors that can cause inflation to rise. If demand for a product outstrips its supply, that can lead to producers raising prices - the craze for Labubu dolls in recent years and the high resale prices are an example. Higher incomes can also lead to higher demand, for example, which in turn pushes up prices. Supply can also affect inflation. If supply of a product is reduced, but demand remains constant, that can cause prices to rise. A good example of this is crude oil, which is used to make gasoline and diesel. Before the US-Israel war with Iran began, it was trading at just over $70 a barrel, but when the conflict constricted crude supplies, the price quickly rose and is currently over $100. What is the current rate of inflation? Over the month of October, prices rose by 0.4%, driven by increases in housing, food and energy costs. However, the pace of energy price rises, at 0.7% in October, was much lower than the 5.2% increase seen in September. While the Bureau of Labor Statistics would normally provide figures for the 12-month change in prices, it did not collect data in October 2025 so it could not provide that estimate. For the 12 months to September, inflation was 3.7%. What does inflation mean for interest rates? The US Federal Reserve has a target for keeping annual inflation at 2%. When inflation is too high the Fed tends to raise interest rates in order to encourage people and businesses to save more and spend less money in the hope this will slow price rises. While there was no annual figure published for inflation this month, analysts say the fact inflation was higher in October than expected increases the chance of an interest rate rise at the Fed's December meeting. Federal Reserve governor Chirstopher Waller, who spoke before the latest inflation figures were published, also suggested he was leaning towards a rate increase in December even if October's figures were slower than expected. - US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you - Published29 October How have tariffs affected inflation? Since coming into office for the second time, President Donald Trump has introduced tariffs on most US trading partners around the world. While most of the additional global levies were outlawed by the Supreme Court in February, the president immediately announced a new 10% global tariff to replace them. Trump argued the tariffs would increase America's tax earnings, boost manufacturing and encourage people to buy US-made goods, but the higher import taxes have also had an impact on inflation, according to research from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. Higher tariffs - which are levies that businesses pay on the goods they import - directly raise prices for US companies unless the overseas firms they are buying from lower prices to absorb some of the cost. In response to the new tariffs, the New York Fed found exporters reduced prices very little, meaning US-based businesses ended up absorbing nearly 90% of the cost of the added tax. Indirectly, higher tariffs also affected the prices of locally made goods, as many US producers rely on parts or materials from overseas. Overall, the Fed found that every percentage point increase in average tariffs led to nearly a 0.25% price increase for consumer goods after one year. Has inflation been worse lately? While inflation is currently above where the Federal Reserve would like it has been much higher in previous years. During the Covid pandemic, issues such as supply chain disruption started pushing inflation up. Additionally, in early 2022 when Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, oil prices surged over $100 a barrel. Both of these factors helped to drive inflation to a peak of about 9%. Can inflation ever go down? It's important to note that if inflation is rising at a slower rate, that does not mean prices are going down - it simply means prices are rising at a slower pace. A bit of inflation is considered good for an economy as the Federal Reserve's target rate illustrates. Many central banks consider inflation of about 2% or a little higher to be stable, and at a level that doesn't impact people's purchasing decisions. Much below that, people can delay spending if they expect price rises to slow further, or to fall. That can lead to businesses reducing wages, or reducing the number of workers to cope with lower demand. How has inflation changed Social Security payments? The value of social security benefits is changed to largely keep up with inflation, protecting people's ability to purchase their usual goods and services through the cost-of-living adjustment. Shortly after September's inflation figure was released, the Social Security Administration announced that Social Security benefits including old age, survivors and disability insurance would rise by a similar amount - 3.6% - in 2027. The administration said that the 3.6% rise will mean an average retirement benefit increase of $75 a month. The cost-of-living adjustment will take effect in January for about 72 million people, while increased payments for the 7.2m receiving the supplemental security income will start on 31 December. Overall, the Fed found that every percentage point increase in average tariffs led to nearly a 0.25% price increase for consumer goods after one year. Has inflation been worse lately? While inflation is currently above where the Federal Reserve would like it has been much higher in previous years. During the Covid pandemic, issues such as supply chain disruption started pushing inflation up. Additionally, in early 2022 when Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, oil prices surged over $100 a barrel. Both of these factors helped to drive inflation to a peak of about 9%. Can inflation ever go down? It's important to note that if inflation is rising at a slower rate, that does not mean prices are going down - it simply means prices are rising at a slower pace. A bit of inflation is considered good for an economy as the Federal Reserve's target rate illustrates. Many central banks consider inflation of about 2% or a little higher to be stable, and at a level that doesn't impact people's purchasing decisions. Much below that, people can delay spending if they expect price rises to slow further, or to fall. That can lead to businesses reducing wages, or reducing the number of workers to cope with lower demand. How has inflation changed Social Security payments? The value of social security benefits is changed to largely keep up with inflation, protecting people's ability to purchase their usual goods and services through the cost-of-living adjustment. Shortly after September's inflation figure was released, the Social Security Administration announced that Social Security benefits including old age, survivors and disability insurance would rise by a similar amount - 3.6% - in 2027. The administration said that the 3.6% rise will mean an average retirement benefit increase of $75 a month. The cost-of-living adjustment will take effect in January for about 72 million people, while increased payments for the 7.2m receiving the supplemental security income will start on 31 December. articles.articleText: Kıvanç Zaimler'den COP31'te finansman uyarısı: "Dönüşüm adil olmalı" - Sabancı Holding CEO'su Kıvanç Zaimler, COP31'in Türkiye için enerji ve iklim dönüşümünü anlatma fırsatı sunduğunu belirterek reel sektörün dönüşüm yatırımlarına istekli olduğunu söyledi. - Zaimler, finansmana erişimde ülkeler ve şirketler arasında adil koşulların sağlanması gerektiğini vurguladı. Sabancı Holding CEO'su Kıvanç Zaimler, CNBC-e canlı yayınında COP31 gündemini ve Türkiye'nin enerji dönüşümündeki fırsatlarını değerlendirdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Türkiye'nin COP31'e ev sahipliği yapmasının ve eş başkanlık görevini üstlenmesinin önemli bir fırsat olduğunu belirten Zaimler, zirvenin Türkiye'nin iklim ve elektrifikasyon alanındaki dönüşümünü uluslararası kamuoyuna anlatmak açısından değer taşıdığını ifade etti. Türkiye'nin enerji bağımlılığını azaltabileceğine dikkat çeken Zaimler, özellikle ham petrol ve doğal gaza bağımlı ülkeler açısından elektrifikasyonun önemli bir dönüşüm alanı olduğunu söyledi. Zaimler, bu süreçte Türkiye'nin teknolojik kabiliyetlerinden ve insan kaynağından yararlanabileceğini kaydetti. "Finansmana adil koşullarda erişilmeli" Reel sektörün yeşil dönüşüm yatırımlarında finansmanın belirleyici rol oynadığını vurgulayan Zaimler, dönüşümün adil şartlarda gerçekleşmesi gerektiğini söyledi. Ülkelerin finansmana erişiminde sermaye maliyetlerinin farklılaşmasına dikkat çeken Zaimler, daha zengin ülkelerin daha düşük maliyetlerle kaynak bulabildiğini, gelişmekte olan ülkelerin ise daha yüksek finansman maliyetleriyle karşılaştığını belirtti. Zaimler, "Bu dönüşümün adil olması lazım. Ülkelerin de reel sektörün de bu finansmana adil şartlarla erişmesi lazım." dedi. Finansman maliyetlerinin yükselmemesi için düzenleyici kurumlara ve politika yapıcılara önemli görevler düştüğünü ifade eden Zaimler, yatırımcıların ihtiyaç duyduğu güven ve öngörülebilirliğin düzenlemeler ve uzun vadeli politikalarla sağlanabileceğini dile getirdi. Finansman sağlayan kuruluşların ticari kaygılarının yanı sıra ekipman tedarikinde menşe ve ülke kısıtlamalarının da süreci etkilediğini belirten Zaimler, bu tür sınırlamaların adil dönüşüm hedefiyle örtüşmediğini söyledi. Zaimler, finansman ihtiyacına rağmen reel sektörde dönüşüm yatırımlarına yönelik güçlü bir istek bulunduğunu kaydetti. Sabancı'nın iki büyüme alanı: Elektrifikasyon ve malzeme teknolojileri Sabancı Holding'in büyüme stratejisinde iki ana alanın öne çıktığını belirten Zaimler, bunları elektrifikasyon ve kritik minerallerden beslenen malzeme teknolojileri olarak sıraladı. Elektrifikasyonun yalnızca elektrik üretimiyle sınırlı olmadığını vurgulayan Zaimler; dağıtım şebekeleri, şarj istasyonları, elektrikli mobilite, otobüs üretimi, sanayide elektrifikasyon ve finansman alanlarının da bu dönüşümün parçası olduğunu söyledi. Akbank'ın dönüşüm yatırımlarının finansmanında rol üstlendiğini, üniversite ve araştırma merkezleriyle de bu alanda faaliyet gösterdiklerini belirten Zaimler, Sabancı'nın COP31'de elektrifikasyon partneri olduğunu hatırlattı. İkinci büyüme alanı olarak malzeme teknolojilerine işaret eden Zaimler, dijital dönüşüm ve teknolojinin kullanımının da bu iki stratejik alanı desteklediğini ifade etti. Elektrifikasyon, ulaşım, sanayi ve enerji gibi alanlarda fosil yakıtların yerine elektrik kullanımının yaygınlaşmasını ifade ediyor. Bu dönüşüm; yenilenebilir enerji üretimi, elektrik şebekeleri, batarya teknolojileri ve şarj altyapısı gibi alanlarda yeni yatırım ihtiyaçları doğuruyor.

articles.title: First day of Ukraine peace talks 'very productive', US says
articles.summary: Delegations from Kyiv, Washington and Moscow are in the United Arab Emirates for the first trilateral talks since February.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: First day of Ukraine peace talks 'very productive', US says
articles.summaryTr: Delegations from Kyiv, Washington and Moscow are in the United Arab Emirates for the first trilateral talks since February.
articles.articleText: First day of Ukraine peace talks 'very productive', US says - Published The first day of trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine has concluded in Abu Dhabi. While senior officials from Kyiv and Moscow were tight-lipped after the four hour-long discussions - due to resume on Wednesday - US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who did not attend the talks, said they had been "very productive". Although expectations for a breakthrough that ends Russia's full-scale war on Ukraine are low, US officials said earlier that Moscow and Kyiv were privately showing "a little bit of flexibility" on the issue of who would control Ukraine's eastern regions in a postwar scenario. At the start of Tuesday's talks President Donald Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner, told delegates that the US had "narrowed the gaps" between the two sides, without providing details, and hoped to move towards a "solution that hopefully ends the war". Kushner said earlier the talks would be focused on addressing the "postwar security concerns" of both Russia and Ukraine. He and Trump peace envoy Steve Witkoff also met Ukrainian and European and Nato officials on the sidelines of the main meeting. European leaders have largely been excluded from peace talks until now, but they have pushed to be included in the discussions amid concerns that decisions about their continent's security would be made without them. The Americans appear to support this, with Rubio acknowledging during a visit to Paris that the Europeans "are a part of solving this problem for the long term". However, "the Russians have a bad taste in their mouth with the Europeans", according to a US official. Some proposals favoured by EU officials - such as calling an unconditional ceasefire as a prerequisite for peace negotiations - are routinely rejected by Moscow. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said on Tuesday that a truce would just allow Kyiv to regroup. "We will not agree to it," he said. Moscow and Kyiv's positions are still far apart on ending the conflict. A key area of disagreement involves Ukraine's eastern region of Donetsk, which is mostly occupied by Russia. Moscow has demanded that Ukraine relinquish the parts of Donetsk it still holds, while Kyiv wants to freeze the contact line to maintain control over those areas, which it says are crucial to its future security. While neither side has budged on these demands, the US official speaking on the eve of the talks suggested that this was just the public stance and that Moscow and Kyiv had shown "a little bit of flexibility, privately". However, he acknowledged the issue would not be solved without discussions about a new "security architecture". "They will not solve the Donetsk issue and the territorial issue until they know what the security architecture is going to be after the war," the official said. "And keep in mind, we're not going to be able to finalise one without the other." For Ukraine, a post-war "security architecture" may include reassurance that allies will come to its aid if it comes under attack again. For Russia, that could be its longstanding ambition to see Nato roll back from Eastern Europe – which would be alarming to Europeans. The framework being proposed includes security consultations and crisis communications hotlines, as well as "reciprocal de-escalation measures" between the two. The officials also floated the re-activation of the Nato-Russia Council that has been largely paused since 2022. The last round of trilateral talks, held in Geneva in February, ended without a breakthrough. Soon after, the US-Israel war on Iran diverted Washington's attention from Ukraine, and no other discussions were held since. From the start of his second term in office, US President Donald Trump – who once boasted he could end the war in Ukraine within a day – has spearheaded several rounds of talks to end the conflict, albeit with little success. Meanwhile, his increasingly conciliatory approach towards Moscow has fuelled deep unease in Kyiv and across the European Union. After meeting Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev in Washington last week, Trump touted a forthcoming "big, beautiful agreement" on Ukraine that "might involve all of Europe". Many in Ukraine are sceptical that this would result in a fair peace. Ukrainian MP Oleksandr Merezhko, head of the foreign affairs parliamentary committee, told the BBC he believed Trump wanted "a quick deal at the expense of Ukraine", which will certainly be rejected by Kyiv. The only way to make Russia's Vladimir Putin start real negotiations was by putting greater pressure on Russia through sanctions and deep strikes, Merezhko said. "While Putin has a war machine up and running, he has no incentives to negotiate." He also mentioned recent moves by Trump, such as his deal to buy diesel from Russia, as something that "only encourages Moscow to continue the war". Moscow's delegation in Abu Dhabi includes Kremlin aide Vladimir Medinsky, deputy foreign ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, spy chief Igor Kostyukov and army general Yury Zhigarlovsky. Kyiv has sent several senior officials who have been part of previous negotiating teams, including Foreign Intelligence Service head Rustem Umerov, Volodymyr Zelensky's chief of staff Kyrylo Budanov, and MP Davyd Arakhamiya. Away from Abu Dhabi, Russia continues to pummel Ukraine with deadly bombardments and strikes on energy infrastructure, viewed in Kyiv as proof that Moscow wants to corner Ukraine into accepting a deal on Russia's terms. On Monday, Kushner was cautious to point out that the Abu Dhabi talks could at most "build momentum toward the next phase of negotiations". "This is an extraordinarily difficult and complicated conflict," he wrote on X, adding the US was "approaching these discussions with determination and realism." articles.title: Arrests made in Mohamed Al Fayed probe in France, police say
articles.summary: The Ritz hotel in Paris, which is still owned by the Al Fayed family, is one of the properties searched by police.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Arrests made in Mohamed Al Fayed probe in France, police say
articles.summaryTr: The Ritz hotel in Paris, which is still owned by the Al Fayed family, is one of the properties searched by police.
articles.articleText: Arrests made in Mohamed Al Fayed probe in France, police say - Published French police have made arrests after three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, were searched in relation to an investigation into Mohamed Al Fayed's abuse. In a confidential letter sent to survivors, the Metropolitan Police confirmed that on 13 and 14 October, French police searched three properties which resulted in a "number of arrests". Met officers were present in what is understood to be a joint operation between British and French authorities. It is the first time any arrests have been made in relation to alleged abuse and trafficking by the former Harrods and Ritz owner. - Mohamed Al Fayed accused of multiple rapes by staff - Published19 September 2024 The Met shared this statement from French authorities with victims: "At this stage of the proceedings, several victims have been interviewed by French investigators, and the investigations are being conducted in liaison with the British authorities. "In this context, searches and evidence-gathering operations were carried out in mid-October 2026, notably within the Hotel Ritz in the 1st arrondissement of Paris, as well as at the Villa Sainte-Thérèse in Saint-Tropez, a former property of Mohamed Al Fayed, and at the Villa Windsor in the 16th arrondissement of Paris, in the presence of British investigators. "Several suspects were taken into police custody, measures which were lifted following their interviews, specifically for the purpose of analyzing digital material seized during the search operations. "The investigations are continuing under the direction of the Paris Public Prosecutor's Office." A Met Police spokesperson confirmed its officers travelled to France in October and were present during the operation. Al Fayed was accused by more than 20 women of sexual assault in a BBC documentary and podcast in September 2024. One of the women featured in the documentary said she was sexually assaulted by Al Fayed at the Ritz hotel in Paris, while another woman said she had been raped by him at the Villa Windsor hotel in Paris. Since those allegations, more than 400 alleged victims or witnesses have come forward to lawyers. The Justice for Fayed and Harrods Survivors group said it welcomed the "significant developments" and cooperation between the Met and French authorities. "We believe that all properties owned by Fayed should be investigated with the same thoroughness as those already searched, wherever they are located, to ensure that no potentially relevant evidence is overlooked," the group said. "We hope these developments represent meaningful progress towards identifying and holding to account all those who facilitated, concealed or assisted his offending, wherever they operated." The survivor advocacy group No One Above said: "France is treating this as organised human trafficking, led by specialists, with properties searched and evidence seized. That is what a serious investigation into a network looks like. "Two years on, survivors are still waiting for the same from the Met. It is time the National Crime Agency took this investigation over." - Published27 September 2024 - Published24 August

"In this context, searches and evidence-gathering operations were carried out in mid-October 2026, notably within the Hotel Ritz in the 1st arrondissement of Paris, as well as at the Villa Sainte-Thérèse in Saint-Tropez, a former property of Mohamed Al Fayed, and at the Villa Windsor in the 16th arrondissement of Paris, in the presence of British investigators. "Several suspects were taken into police custody, measures which were lifted following their interviews, specifically for the purpose of analyzing digital material seized during the search operations. "The investigations are continuing under the direction of the Paris Public Prosecutor's Office." A Met Police spokesperson confirmed its officers travelled to France in October and were present during the operation. Al Fayed was accused by more than 20 women of sexual assault in a BBC documentary and podcast in September 2024. One of the women featured in the documentary said she was sexually assaulted by Al Fayed at the Ritz hotel in Paris, while another woman said she had been raped by him at the Villa Windsor hotel in Paris. Since those allegations, more than 400 alleged victims or witnesses have come forward to lawyers. The Justice for Fayed and Harrods Survivors group said it welcomed the "significant developments" and cooperation between the Met and French authorities. "We believe that all properties owned by Fayed should be investigated with the same thoroughness as those already searched, wherever they are located, to ensure that no potentially relevant evidence is overlooked," the group said. "We hope these developments represent meaningful progress towards identifying and holding to account all those who facilitated, concealed or assisted his offending, wherever they operated." The survivor advocacy group No One Above said: "France is treating this as organised human trafficking, led by specialists, with properties searched and evidence seized. That is what a serious investigation into a network looks like. "Two years on, survivors are still waiting for the same from the Met. It is time the National Crime Agency took this investigation over." - Published27 September 2024 - Published24 August

articles.summaryTr: ABD'de ekim ayı enflasyonunun beklentileri aşması ve Fed'in faiz artışına yönelik beklentilerin güçlenmesiyle spot altının ons fiyatı TSİ 17.00 itibarıyla yüzde 2'den fazla düşerek 4 bin 55 dolara geriledi.
articles.articleText: ABD enflasyonu altını vurdu: Fiyatlar yüzde 2'den fazla geriledi ABD'de ekim ayı enflasyonunun beklentileri aşması ve Fed'in faiz artışına yönelik beklentilerin güçlenmesiyle spot altının ons fiyatı TSİ 17.00 itibarıyla yüzde 2'den fazla düşerek 4 bin 55 dolara geriledi. ABD'de ekim ayı enflasyonunun beklentilerin üzerinde gerçekleşmesi ve Fed'in faiz artışına yönelik beklentilerin güçlenmesiyle altın fiyatları yüzde 2'den fazla geriledi. Spot altının ons fiyatı TSİ 17.00 itibarıyla yüzde 2 düşüşle 4.055 dolar dolara indi. Enflasyon verisinin ardından yatırımcıların Fed'in aralık ayında daha güçlü bir faiz artışına gidebileceği beklentisiyle satışlarını artırdığı belirtildi. ABD'de enflasyon beklentileri aştı ABD Çalışma İstatistikleri Bürosunun (BLS) açıkladığı verilere göre, Tüketici Fiyat Endeksi (TÜFE) ekimde aylık bazda yüzde 0,4 yükseldi. Ekonomistlerin beklentisi yüzde 0,3 artış yönündeydi. Eylülde aylık enflasyon yüzde 0,6 olarak kaydedilmişti. Gıda ve enerji fiyatlarının hariç tutulduğu çekirdek TÜFE ise ekimde yüzde 0,3 arttı. Böylece çekirdek enflasyondaki aylık artış eylül ayındaki seviyesini korurken, piyasa beklentisi yüzde 0,2 düzeyindeydi. Ekim ayı yıllık enflasyonu hesaplanamadı BLS, geçen yıl hükümetin kapanması nedeniyle Ekim 2025 döneminde anket verisi toplayamadığını ve birçok TÜFE endeksi için ilgili ayın verilerini yayımlayamadığını bildirdi. Bu nedenle kurum, Ekim 2026 için bazı endekslerde yıllık değişim oranlarını hesaplayamadı. Altın fiyatları, enflasyon verisi öncesinde de Fed Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi Christopher Waller'ın açıklamalarının etkisiyle baskı altındaydı. Waller, enflasyon görünümünün kötüleşmesi halinde aralık ayında 50 baz puanlık faiz artışının değerlendirilmesi gerektiğini belirtmişti.

articles.title: Iran rejects French claims it was behind supermarket fridge hacking
articles.summary: Tons of chilled and frozen food was spoiled last month as fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets heated up.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Iran rejects French claims it was behind supermarket fridge hacking
articles.summaryTr: Tons of chilled and frozen food was spoiled last month as fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets heated up.
articles.articleText: Iran rejects French claims it was behind supermarket fridge hacking - Published Iran has described French accusations that it was behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers as "baseless and hostile". On Monday, the French authorities blamed Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) for the string of hacks, which foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot said were "unprecedented" in terms of their scale and "level of aggression". He added that those responsible would be hit with sanctions. The French cyber-attacks, which led to the destruction of tons of frozen and chilled food, were followed by a similar hacks against supermarkets across several other European countries. It is not known if the instances are linked. Barrot said the attack on France's supermarkets "marks the first large-scale cyber-attack aimed at sabotage on our national territory, and it constitutes a major attack on the nation's interests and the security of the French people". He said the government had summoned the Iranian ambassador to Paris to "lodge a very strong protest against this extremely grave act". France will take "any other necessary and proportionate measures" to respond to the incident and "deter anyone who might seek to repeat it", Barrot added. The Paris prosecutor, Laure Beccuau, said an investigation had been opened into the head of an offensive cyber unit associated with the IRGC as well as his two deputies. Beccuau named the unit as Shahid Kaveh, which she said had an affiliation with the electronic and cyber centre of the IRGC. Shahid Kaveh is the name given to a cluster of hackers thought to be directly employed by the Iranian regime. In recent weeks, a number of commentators and politicians in Iran have argued that the country should extend any retaliation beyond the Middle East if the US and Israel resume the war they started earlier this year. On Monday, some Iranian media outlets denied the French accusations, but there had been no official comment until Tuesday's statement from Iran's foreign ministry. On 11 October, hackers gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units used in many of France's supermarkets. More than 100 of Coopérative U's supermarkets were hit, as well as 180 stores from Intermarché and its Netto brand. In some stores, temperatures of the fridges reportedly rose to 50C (120F) overnight. Other major food retailers including Carrefour, Monoprix and E.Leclerc were also hit by the attack, which targeted software provided by Danish engineering firm Danfoss. The software allows retailers to manage their cold units remotely. Earlier this month a second wave of hacks took place, hitting more than 100 stores across Europe. Supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, while a smaller number of shops were hit in countries including Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland. Separately in August a small number of US military bases had fridges mysteriously malfunction, spoiling food. This incident is also being investigated as deliberate cyber-attacks, Reuters news agency has reported, citing sources familiar with the matter. Since the waves of attacks on freezers, experts have been speculating which hacking groups could be responsible, with Iran being on a list of potential suspects. In spite of a pair of Russian-aligned hacktivist groups claiming they were responsible on Wednesday, few believed them. The French government has not said how it reached the conclusion that Iran was responsible, and attribution of cyber-attacks is extremely hard as hackers are able to hide their locations. Additional reporting by Farshad Bayan, BBC Persian. Related topics - Published2 November

articles.title: New regulation for heating oil market, but no price controls
articles.summary: The Competition and Markets Authority has investigated the heating oil market in Northern Ireland and other parts of the UK.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: New regulation for heating oil market, but no price controls
articles.summaryTr: The Competition and Markets Authority has investigated the heating oil market in Northern Ireland and other parts of the UK.
articles.articleText: New regulation for heating oil market, but no price controls - Published Home heating oil suppliers in Northern Ireland will face stricter regulation in the wake of an inquiry by the UK's competition watchdog. However it will not include the sort of price controls applied to the gas and electricity markets. The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) investigated the heating oil market in Northern Ireland and other parts of the UK., external The Economy Minister Caoimhe Archibald said she will now act on the CMA's recommendations. "The CMA identified the need for stronger consumer protection, support for vulnerable households, and more formal dispute resolution arrangements," she told MLAs. She said the changes she was announcing are "proportionate" and will enhance existing heating oil consumer protection "at minimal additional cost". What regulations will be put in place for home heating oil? The measures include a mandatory code of conduct for heating oil suppliers and giving the Consumer Council an enhanced role in helping consumers resolve disputes. The Consumer Council will also lead in the creation of an opt-in register for vulnerable consumers. About two thirds of Northern Ireland households use home heating oil, by far the highest of any UK region. At the start of the US-Israel attack on Iran in March, heating oil prices in Northern Ireland rose by a record monthly rate of 92%. That compared to the previous largest spike of 59% in March 2022, after the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Analysis by the CMA suggested that prices rose even more steeply in Scotland and Wales, where heating oil is typically used in remote rural areas. It found that prices tended to be lower in Northern Ireland overall as it has a competitive range of suppliers and a market which is big enough to minimise delivery costs. The CMA said that the huge spike in prices at the start of the Iran conflict largely reflected rising wholesale costs. It did not recommend price controls suggesting they could be counterproductive. - Published9 September - Published14 September - Published28 September

articles.title: Poland’s lower house backs sanctions bill covering crypto freezes
articles.summary: The bill is now before the Senate and would broaden the grounds for adding people and companies to Poland’s national sanctions list.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Poland’s lower house backs sanctions bill covering crypto freezes
articles.summaryTr: The bill is now before the Senate and would broaden the grounds for adding people and companies to Poland’s national sanctions list.
articles.articleText: Poland’s lower house backs sanctions bill covering crypto freezes The bill is now before the Senate and would broaden the grounds for adding people and companies to Poland’s national sanctions list. Poland’s lower house passed a bill that would broaden the country’s sanctions framework and explicitly include crypto assets among the funds authorities can freeze when imposing sanctions. The Sejm approved the government-backed Act on Restrictive Measures on Friday by 240 votes to 202, with one abstention, and forwarded it to the Senate on Monday, according to official parliamentary records. The bill explicitly includes crypto assets, as defined under the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), among financial funds that authorities could freeze when imposing sanctions. Poland’s interior minister would oversee the national sanctions list, with sanctions-listing decisions taking effect the day after authorities publish a designation. Affected individuals and companies could challenge the decision in administrative court, but the bill allows enforcement before a court ruling. Poland already maintains a national sanctions list under a 2022 law aimed at countering support for Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. The bill would expand the grounds for imposing national sanctions to include certain foreign interference and information manipulation that pose a serious threat to national security. The Senate has 30 days to approve, amend or reject the legislation. If it takes no action, Poland’s Constitution treats the bill as approved in the form passed by the Sejm, allowing it to proceed to the president for consideration. Related: US Treasury cuts off MEXC over alleged $16B in illicit transactions

articles.title: Civil servant who secretly held five jobs found guilty of fraud
articles.summary: Kashim Chowdhury had secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Civil servant who secretly held five jobs found guilty of fraud
articles.summaryTr: Kashim Chowdhury had secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries.
articles.articleText: Civil servant who secretly held five jobs found guilty of fraud - Published A civil servant who secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries has been found guilty of nine counts of fraud. Kashim Chowdhury, from east London, had five government jobs that overlapped in the spring of 2023. He fraudulently earned more than £284,000 of taxpayers' money. The prosecution accused the 56-year-old of ''deliberate, intentional dishonesty'' and of ''exploiting the system''. After seven hours of deliberation, the jury unanimously found Chowdhury guilty of eight counts of fraud by false representation and one count of fraud by a failure to disclose. The judge said Chowdhury faced a ''very significant custodial sentence''. He added he was refusing bail because of the significance of the crime and for Chowdhury's own wellbeing. 'Abused trust' "This was sustained and deliberate dishonesty," said Sarah Melo, specialist prosecutor at the CPS Serious Economic Organised Crime and International Directorate. "He knew he could not legitimately hold multiple full-time positions at the same time, but continued to conceal what he was doing." A Defra spokesperson said Chowdury "abused the trust placed in him as a public servant", adding that it would use all available avenues to recover the proceeds of Chowdhury's offending. Between 2020 and 2023 Chowdhury had eight full-time public sector roles that overlapped and earned him £350,000 in total. The prosecution told the court that on application forms he provided inaccurate information about his employment status and failed to disclose to government departments that he was already a civil servant. Once he secured the roles he didn't tell his employers he was working elsewhere. He was allowed to work entirely from home because he told his employers he was caring for his mother, whom he lived with in east London. She had dementia and was diagnosed with terminal cancer in 2023. - How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long - Published20 hours ago But rather than reduce his workload to look after her, he kept taking on new jobs. In the spring of 2023, when his mother was a few months away from death, he had jobs at the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, the Department of Health and Social Care, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), the Department for Business and Trade, the Food Standards Agency and the Home Office. During this period he was contracted to work 183 hours a week - more than the number of hours that exist in seven days. Chowdhury said he had taken on so many roles because he feared losing his livelihood after experiencing insecure employment in the past. He was made redundant from a job at the Department for Education in 2013 and was given a diagnosis of PTSD. He said he had not been thinking clearly when applying for jobs ''because of my stress, distress and trauma and due to my panic at the time". But the prosecution barrister, Lucy Organ, told the jury: "He's lied to you in evidence, he's lied to you under oath, which demonstrates the level of deceit he has descended to." A succession of his managers told the court about his poor performance. Especially damning was the evidence given by Dan McCartney who managed Chowdhury at Defra. He said he had to "effectively tell him what to do the whole time". McCartney said that during video calls Chowdhury had his camera switched off blaming technical problems. McCartney said this went on for four to five months. But McCartney said that because Chowdhury was not subject to any formal performance measures at Defra, he was given a permanent job and remained there for two years. The prosecution argued that he used sick notes to cope with his impossible schedule. In March 2023, he was on sick leave from four of the organisations he worked for. But he kept working at the Home Office and did not tell them he was ill. His line manager at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), Aleesha Adams, organised a video call with him in May 2023. By this point he'd been off sick for three months and she wanted to make a plan to get him back to work. She told the jury that at the start of the call he was coughing a lot and waving tissues up to the camera. She also told the jury that he had been wearing white make-up to try to look ill. Adams told the court that as the meeting went on the make-up started coming off his forehead. ''He was sweating, it was like rubbing off so it was darker underneath and darker on the neck." Chowdhury told the jury this was a smear and that he had not been wearing make-up. After the call, Adams discovered that he had logged into the call using a Defra email address. When she challenged him about it he blamed a technical error. Adams grew suspicious. ''I believed he was lying,'' she told the jury. She escalated her concerns up the chain at the UKHSA. But his fraudulent behaviour went on for several more months. The government's National Fraud Initiative flagged suspected fraud to Defra in 2023. Following this, the Defra Investigations Team launched an investigation and as a result, Chowdhury was arrested and interviewed under caution in July 2023. He was dismissed by the civil service in September 2023. Chowdhury has also been accused by his siblings of bullying their mother into increasing his share of the family home days before she died. In a case at the High Court, Chowdhury's two brothers and sister allege that he put "undue influence" on Faijun Nessa to sign documents that meant he would inherit half of her home. The four-storey, six-bedroom home in east London has been valued at £2.1m. His siblings say their mother could not have understood what she was signing because she was "desperately unwell". In January 2023 she was given a terminal diagnosis of stage four metastatic colorectal cancer. The claimants also allege that Mrs Nessa, who was nearly blind and could not speak English, was unaware of what she was signing because the documents were not translated into her native Bengali at the time they were signed. Kashim Chowdhury denies the claims. That case is ongoing. Additional reporting by Ben Sturt.
articles.articleTextTr: Civil servant who secretly held five jobs found guilty of fraud - Published A civil servant who secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries has been found guilty of nine counts of fraud. Kashim Chowdhury, from east London, had five government jobs that overlapped in the spring of 2023. He fraudulently earned more than £284,000 of taxpayers' money. The prosecution accused the 56-year-old of ''deliberate, intentional dishonesty'' and of ''exploiting the system''. After seven hours of deliberation, the jury unanimously found Chowdhury guilty of eight counts of fraud by false representation and one count of fraud by a failure to disclose. The judge said Chowdhury faced a ''very significant custodial sentence''. He added he was refusing bail because of the significance of the crime and for Chowdhury's own wellbeing. 'Abused trust' "This was sustained and deliberate dishonesty," said Sarah Melo, specialist prosecutor at the CPS Serious Economic Organised Crime and International Directorate. "He knew he could not legitimately hold multiple full-time positions at the same time, but continued to conceal what he was doing." A Defra spokesperson said Chowdury "abused the trust placed in him as a public servant", adding that it would use all available avenues to recover the proceeds of Chowdhury's offending. Between 2020 and 2023 Chowdhury had eight full-time public sector roles that overlapped and earned him £350,000 in total. The prosecution told the court that on application forms he provided inaccurate information about his employment status and failed to disclose to government departments that he was already a civil servant. Once he secured the roles he didn't tell his employers he was working elsewhere. He was allowed to work entirely from home because he told his employers he was caring for his mother, whom he lived with in east London. She had dementia and was diagnosed with terminal cancer in 2023. - How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long - Published20 hours ago But rather than reduce his workload to look after her, he kept taking on new jobs. In the spring of 2023, when his mother was a few months away from death, he had jobs at the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, the Department of Health and Social Care, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), the Department for Business and Trade, the Food Standards Agency and the Home Office. During this period he was contracted to work 183 hours a week - more than the number of hours that exist in seven days. Chowdhury said he had taken on so many roles because he feared losing his livelihood after experiencing insecure employment in the past. He was made redundant from a job at the Department for Education in 2013 and was given a diagnosis of PTSD. He said he had not been thinking clearly when applying for jobs ''because of my stress, distress and trauma and due to my panic at the time". But the prosecution barrister, Lucy Organ, told the jury: "He's lied to you in evidence, he's lied to you under oath, which demonstrates the level of deceit he has descended to." A succession of his managers told the court about his poor performance. Especially damning was the evidence given by Dan McCartney who managed Chowdhury at Defra. He said he had to "effectively tell him what to do the whole time". McCartney said that during video calls Chowdhury had his camera switched off blaming technical problems. McCartney said this went on for four to five months. But McCartney said that because Chowdhury was not subject to any formal performance measures at Defra, he was given a permanent job and remained there for two years. The prosecution argued that he used sick notes to cope with his impossible schedule. In March 2023, he was on sick leave from four of the organisations he worked for. But he kept working at the Home Office and did not tell them he was ill. His line manager at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), Aleesha Adams, organised a video call with him in May 2023. By this point he'd been off sick for three months and she wanted to make a plan to get him back to work. She told the jury that at the start of the call he was coughing a lot and waving tissues up to the camera. She also told the jury that he had been wearing white make-up to try to look ill. Adams told the court that as the meeting went on the make-up started coming off his forehead. ''He was sweating, it was like rubbing off so it was darker underneath and darker on the neck." Chowdhury told the jury this was a smear and that he had not been wearing make-up. After the call, Adams discovered that he had logged into the call using a Defra email address. When she challenged him about it he blamed a technical error. Adams grew suspicious. ''I believed he was lying,'' she told the jury. She escalated her concerns up the chain at the UKHSA. But his fraudulent behaviour went on for several more months. The government's National Fraud Initiative flagged suspected fraud to Defra in 2023. Following this, the Defra Investigations Team launched an investigation and as a result, Chowdhury was arrested and interviewed under caution in July 2023. He was dismissed by the civil service in September 2023. Chowdhury has also been accused by his siblings of bullying their mother into increasing his share of the family home days before she died. In a case at the High Court, Chowdhury's two brothers and sister allege that he put "undue influence" on Faijun Nessa to sign documents that meant he would inherit half of her home. The four-storey, six-bedroom home in east London has been valued at £2.1m. His siblings say their mother could not have understood what she was signing because she was "desperately unwell". In January 2023 she was given a terminal diagnosis of stage four metastatic colorectal cancer. The claimants also allege that Mrs Nessa, who was nearly blind and could not speak English, was unaware of what she was signing because the documents were not translated into her native Bengali at the time they were signed. Kashim Chowdhury denies the claims. That case is ongoing. Additional reporting by Ben Sturt.

articles.articleText: İran'dan savaş resti: "ABD ve İsrail'i bekleyen sürprizler var" - İran Genelkurmay Başkanı Tümgeneral Ali Abdullahi, ABD ve İsrail'le olası yeni bir çatışmada "birçok sürprizin ardı ardına ortaya çıkacağını" söyledi. - Abdullahi, İran'ın hedef alınması halinde karşılık vereceklerini belirtti. İran ile ABD ve İsrail arasındaki gerilim sürerken Tahran'dan yeni bir açıklama geldi. İran Genelkurmay Başkanı Tümgeneral Ali Abdullahi, olası bir savaşın yeniden başlaması halinde karşı tarafı bekleyen sürprizler olacağını ifade etti. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle İran resmi haber ajansı IRNA'nın aktardığına göre Abdullahi, Devrim Muhafızları Ordusunun yeni yer altı füze üssünün tanıtım töreninde konuştu. ABD ve İsrail'in tehditlerine değinen Abdullahi, düşmanın askeri gücünün ve sahip olduğu tesislerin İran'ın kararlarını etkilemeyeceğini söyledi. "Gelecekteki savaşta sürprizler olacak" İsrail Başbakanı Binyamin Netanyahu'nun İran'a yönelik açıklamalarına da yanıt veren Abdullahi, Netanyahu'nun "Ya İran'ı yok edeceğiz ya da İran bizi yok edecek" sözlerini hatırlattı. Abdullahi, İran'ın bu tehditlere boyun eğmeyeceğini belirterek, "Onları kesinlikle yok edeceğimiz açıktır" ifadelerini kullandı. İranlı komutan, önceki çatışmalarda ABD ve İsrail'in sahip oldukları askeri imkanları kullandıklarını ancak hedeflerine ulaşamadıklarını öne sürdü. Abdullahi, konuşmasını olası yeni çatışmaya ilişkin şu sözlerle tamamladı: "Gelecekteki savaşta sürprizler ardı ardına ortaya çıkacak."

articles.summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

articles.titleTr: Here’s what happened in crypto today
articles.summaryTr: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
articles.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, Coinbase and Kalshi have joined four other firms backing the CFTC in a lawsuit over whether US exchanges can list perpetual futures tied to individual stocks, cybersecurity firm CertiK urged exchanges to impose hard dollar limits on hot-wallet holdings following the $6.3 billion Binance hack, and blockchain analytics firm Elliptic reported that North Korean hackers used newly created memecoins to launder stolen funds. Coinbase, Kalshi join lawsuit backing CFTC over US stock perp futures Coinbase, Kalshi and four other companies asked a federal court Monday to accept a brief backing the United States Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) in a lawsuit over perpetual futures tied to individual US stocks. According to a proposed amicus brief shared Monday by Coinbase legal representative Molly Abraham, the group also includes Kraken parent Payward, trading companies DRW Holdings and Jump Trading, and crypto investment company Paradigm Operations. The companies argue that stock perpetual futures fall under existing US futures laws. The filing comes days after a federal judge found that the CFTC likely “exceeded its statutory authority” in allowing single-stock perpetuals to trade as security futures. The case could determine whether US exchanges can offer retail traders contracts that track individual stocks without expiring. On Nov. 3, the CFTC announced that single-stock perpetual futures, or stock perps, could begin trading on US-regulated exchanges for the first time. The Capital Markets Alliance Association (CMAA), a newly formed trade and advocacy group representing traditional financial market participants and whose members include Cboe and Citadel Securities, sued the CFTC last week, challenging the CFTC’s authority to allow the contracts to trade. Crypto exchanges need dollar caps on hot wallets, CertiK says Crypto exchanges should impose hard dollar limits on their hot-wallet holdings rather than relying solely on cold-storage ratios to measure security, according to cybersecurity firm CertiK. The recommendation came as several crypto exchanges recently disclosed how much they held in cold wallets, seeking to reassure customers after the record Binance hack that targeted its hot wallets. Crypto exchange Gate reported that 88.26% of its total assets were in cold storage, while Coinbase said it keeps more than 99% of customer assets offline. “Cold storage is a useful measure of online exposure, but it is not a standalone security score,” CertiK’s research team told Cointelegraph. CertiK said crypto exchanges should consider setting hot-wallet caps for each asset and blockchain according to the strictest of three limits: a percentage of customer liabilities, estimated withdrawal needs and an absolute loss ceiling based on the exchange’s financial resources and recovery capabilities. “Flexibility should support operating liquidity, while hard dollar ceilings and circuit breakers limit potential loss,” they said. North Korean hackers create memecoins to launder funds from Binance hack: Elliptic North Korean hackers created memecoins to launder cryptocurrency stolen in the $6.3 billion Binance hack, routing roughly $430,000 through six newly launched tokens on the NEAR blockchain, according to a report from blockchain analytics firm Elliptic. Between Nov. 5 and 7, the hackers created at least six tokens on NEAR and used liquidity pools on decentralized exchanges to move stolen funds between wallets, Elliptic said. The tokens attracted almost no outside trading and were abandoned shortly after launch. The hackers used one set of wallets to swap stolen NEAR tokens for the new memecoins, then used another set to sell those memecoins back into the pools for NEAR. The swaps let them move funds without direct wallet-to-wallet transfers, though the transactions remained traceable onchain. Elliptic said the same laundering technique was also used following the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in 2025, when North Korean-linked actors moved at least $24 million through a newly created token on the TRON blockchain.

articles.title: Bitcoin’s ‘best buying opportunity ever’ has arrived: Mark Moss
articles.summary: Bitcoin Opportunity Fund co-founder Mark Moss says that with banks and ETFs widening access to Bitcoin he expects a new record high in 2027.
