news.titleTr: Anthropic heads for lower than expected $1.3 trillion valuation in stock market debut
news.summaryTr: The AI company behind the Claude chatbot will offer its shares at between $70 and $78.
news.articleText: Anthropic heads for lower than expected $1.3 trillion valuation in stock market debut - Published Anthropic, the AI company behind the Claude chatbot, could be valued at around $1.3 trillion (£1 trillion) when it lists its shares for sale on New York's Nasdaq stock exchange. The loss-making company says it will offer its shares for between $70 and $78 each and will raise up to $64bn when it floats this month. It would value Anthropic at between $1.1tn and $1.3tn which, although large, is below the $2tn some backers of the firm predicted in summer, according to the Financial Times. It is floating at a volatile time for AI firms. After last week's US midterm elections, the Nasdaq fell sharply on concerns a Democrat-led Congress could slow development of AI and the buildout of data centres. There are also wider fears over the billions of dollars being spent on AI and whether it will pay off. In its most recent results for the six months to the end of June, Anthropic's revenues jumped to $16.2bn from $1.1bn in the same period last year. However, its pre-tax loss jumped to $80.7bn from $12.9bn. Fiona Cincotta, a senior market analyst at City Index, said the $64bn Anthropic wants to raise is "fairly bullish" within "the volatility [and] concerns towards AI that we've seen in sort of particularly last week". She told Reuters: "It's showing that they are still sort of upbeat about the outlook as far as AI is concerned and that obviously that they think that the demand is going to be there." At $1.3tn, Anthropic's possible valuation is below SpaceX, Elon Musk's rocket, satellite and artificial intelligence company, which listed its shares in June and was valued at nearly $1.8tn. Anthropic is just five years old. It was co-founded in 2021 by brother and sister Dario and Daniela Amodei along with five others - all of whom worked at OpenAI, the rival AI giant behind ChatGPT. news.title: US inflation higher than expected in October - here's what is happening with prices
news.summary: Prices rose by 0.4% over the month, driven by increases in shelter, food and energy costs.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: US inflation higher than expected in October - here's what is happening with prices
news.summaryTr: Prices rose by 0.4% over the month, driven by increases in shelter, food and energy costs.
news.articleText: US inflation higher than expected in October - here's what is happening with prices - Published US inflation rose at a faster-than-expected pace in October, according to official figures. Prices rose by 0.4% in the month, which was lower than the 0.6% increase in September. However, analysts had expected prices to rise by 0.3%, and the higher-than-expected pace could add to arguments for the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at its next meeting in December. The new figures come a week after the midterm elections which were fought over cost-of-living pressures across the US. What is inflation? Inflation is the rate at which the price of products or services increases over time. For example, if a bottle of milk costs $1 but rises to $1.10 a year later, then annual inflation for bottled milk is 10%. Officials from the Bureau of Labor Statistics measure inflation through the consumer price index (CPI). It tracks the price changes of hundreds of day-to-day items including fresh food, gasoline and medical services to work out the overall level of inflation in the US economy. The bureau updates this so-called basket of goods over time as peoples' spending and lifestyle habits change. What causes inflation? There are several factors that can cause inflation to rise. If demand for a product outstrips its supply, that can lead to producers raising prices - the craze for Labubu dolls in recent years and the high resale prices are an example. Higher incomes can also lead to higher demand, for example, which in turn pushes up prices. Supply can also affect inflation. If supply of a product is reduced, but demand remains constant, that can cause prices to rise. A good example of this is crude oil, which is used to make gasoline and diesel. Before the US-Israel war with Iran began, it was trading at just over $70 a barrel, but when the conflict constricted crude supplies, the price quickly rose and is currently over $100. What is the current rate of inflation? Over the month of October, prices rose by 0.4%, driven by increases in housing, food and energy costs. However, the pace of energy price rises, at 0.7% in October, was much lower than the 5.2% increase seen in September. While the Bureau of Labor Statistics would normally provide figures for the 12-month change in prices, it did not collect data in October 2025 so it could not provide that estimate. For the 12 months to September, inflation was 3.7%. What does inflation mean for interest rates? The US Federal Reserve has a target for keeping annual inflation at 2%. When inflation is too high the Fed tends to raise interest rates in order to encourage people and businesses to save more and spend less money in the hope this will slow price rises. While there was no annual figure published for inflation this month, analysts say the fact inflation was higher in October than expected increases the chance of an interest rate rise at the Fed's December meeting. Federal Reserve governor Chirstopher Waller, who spoke before the latest inflation figures were published, also suggested he was leaning towards a rate increase in December even if October's figures were slower than expected. - US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you - Published29 October How have tariffs affected inflation? Since coming into office for the second time, President Donald Trump has introduced tariffs on most US trading partners around the world. While most of the additional global levies were outlawed by the Supreme Court in February, the president immediately announced a new 10% global tariff to replace them. Trump argued the tariffs would increase America's tax earnings, boost manufacturing and encourage people to buy US-made goods, but the higher import taxes have also had an impact on inflation, according to research from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. Higher tariffs - which are levies that businesses pay on the goods they import - directly raise prices for US companies unless the overseas firms they are buying from lower prices to absorb some of the cost. In response to the new tariffs, the New York Fed found exporters reduced prices very little, meaning US-based businesses ended up absorbing nearly 90% of the cost of the added tax. Indirectly, higher tariffs also affected the prices of locally made goods, as many US producers rely on parts or materials from overseas. Overall, the Fed found that every percentage point increase in average tariffs led to nearly a 0.25% price increase for consumer goods after one year. Has inflation been worse lately? While inflation is currently above where the Federal Reserve would like it has been much higher in previous years. During the Covid pandemic, issues such as supply chain disruption started pushing inflation up. Additionally, in early 2022 when Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, oil prices surged over $100 a barrel. Both of these factors helped to drive inflation to a peak of about 9%. Can inflation ever go down? It's important to note that if inflation is rising at a slower rate, that does not mean prices are going down - it simply means prices are rising at a slower pace. A bit of inflation is considered good for an economy as the Federal Reserve's target rate illustrates. Many central banks consider inflation of about 2% or a little higher to be stable, and at a level that doesn't impact people's purchasing decisions. Much below that, people can delay spending if they expect price rises to slow further, or to fall. That can lead to businesses reducing wages, or reducing the number of workers to cope with lower demand. How has inflation changed Social Security payments? The value of social security benefits is changed to largely keep up with inflation, protecting people's ability to purchase their usual goods and services through the cost-of-living adjustment. Shortly after September's inflation figure was released, the Social Security Administration announced that Social Security benefits including old age, survivors and disability insurance would rise by a similar amount - 3.6% - in 2027. The administration said that the 3.6% rise will mean an average retirement benefit increase of $75 a month. The cost-of-living adjustment will take effect in January for about 72 million people, while increased payments for the 7.2m receiving the supplemental security income will start on 31 December. The value of social security benefits is changed to largely keep up with inflation, protecting people's ability to purchase their usual goods and services through the cost-of-living adjustment. Shortly after September's inflation figure was released, the Social Security Administration announced that Social Security benefits including old age, survivors and disability insurance would rise by a similar amount - 3.6% - in 2027. The administration said that the 3.6% rise will mean an average retirement benefit increase of $75 a month. The cost-of-living adjustment will take effect in January for about 72 million people, while increased payments for the 7.2m receiving the supplemental security income will start on 31 December. news.articleText: Kıvanç Zaimler'den COP31'te finansman uyarısı: "Dönüşüm adil olmalı" - Sabancı Holding CEO'su Kıvanç Zaimler, COP31'in Türkiye için enerji ve iklim dönüşümünü anlatma fırsatı sunduğunu belirterek reel sektörün dönüşüm yatırımlarına istekli olduğunu söyledi. - Zaimler, finansmana erişimde ülkeler ve şirketler arasında adil koşulların sağlanması gerektiğini vurguladı. Sabancı Holding CEO'su Kıvanç Zaimler, CNBC-e canlı yayınında COP31 gündemini ve Türkiye'nin enerji dönüşümündeki fırsatlarını değerlendirdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Türkiye'nin COP31'e ev sahipliği yapmasının ve eş başkanlık görevini üstlenmesinin önemli bir fırsat olduğunu belirten Zaimler, zirvenin Türkiye'nin iklim ve elektrifikasyon alanındaki dönüşümünü uluslararası kamuoyuna anlatmak açısından değer taşıdığını ifade etti. Türkiye'nin enerji bağımlılığını azaltabileceğine dikkat çeken Zaimler, özellikle ham petrol ve doğal gaza bağımlı ülkeler açısından elektrifikasyonun önemli bir dönüşüm alanı olduğunu söyledi. Zaimler, bu süreçte Türkiye'nin teknolojik kabiliyetlerinden ve insan kaynağından yararlanabileceğini kaydetti. "Finansmana adil koşullarda erişilmeli" Reel sektörün yeşil dönüşüm yatırımlarında finansmanın belirleyici rol oynadığını vurgulayan Zaimler, dönüşümün adil şartlarda gerçekleşmesi gerektiğini söyledi. Ülkelerin finansmana erişiminde sermaye maliyetlerinin farklılaşmasına dikkat çeken Zaimler, daha zengin ülkelerin daha düşük maliyetlerle kaynak bulabildiğini, gelişmekte olan ülkelerin ise daha yüksek finansman maliyetleriyle karşılaştığını belirtti. Zaimler, "Bu dönüşümün adil olması lazım. Ülkelerin de reel sektörün de bu finansmana adil şartlarla erişmesi lazım." dedi. Finansman maliyetlerinin yükselmemesi için düzenleyici kurumlara ve politika yapıcılara önemli görevler düştüğünü ifade eden Zaimler, yatırımcıların ihtiyaç duyduğu güven ve öngörülebilirliğin düzenlemeler ve uzun vadeli politikalarla sağlanabileceğini dile getirdi. Finansman sağlayan kuruluşların ticari kaygılarının yanı sıra ekipman tedarikinde menşe ve ülke kısıtlamalarının da süreci etkilediğini belirten Zaimler, bu tür sınırlamaların adil dönüşüm hedefiyle örtüşmediğini söyledi. Zaimler, finansman ihtiyacına rağmen reel sektörde dönüşüm yatırımlarına yönelik güçlü bir istek bulunduğunu kaydetti. Sabancı'nın iki büyüme alanı: Elektrifikasyon ve malzeme teknolojileri Sabancı Holding'in büyüme stratejisinde iki ana alanın öne çıktığını belirten Zaimler, bunları elektrifikasyon ve kritik minerallerden beslenen malzeme teknolojileri olarak sıraladı. Elektrifikasyonun yalnızca elektrik üretimiyle sınırlı olmadığını vurgulayan Zaimler; dağıtım şebekeleri, şarj istasyonları, elektrikli mobilite, otobüs üretimi, sanayide elektrifikasyon ve finansman alanlarının da bu dönüşümün parçası olduğunu söyledi. Akbank'ın dönüşüm yatırımlarının finansmanında rol üstlendiğini, üniversite ve araştırma merkezleriyle de bu alanda faaliyet gösterdiklerini belirten Zaimler, Sabancı'nın COP31'de elektrifikasyon partneri olduğunu hatırlattı. İkinci büyüme alanı olarak malzeme teknolojilerine işaret eden Zaimler, dijital dönüşüm ve teknolojinin kullanımının da bu iki stratejik alanı desteklediğini ifade etti. Elektrifikasyon, ulaşım, sanayi ve enerji gibi alanlarda fosil yakıtların yerine elektrik kullanımının yaygınlaşmasını ifade ediyor. Bu dönüşüm; yenilenebilir enerji üretimi, elektrik şebekeleri, batarya teknolojileri ve şarj altyapısı gibi alanlarda yeni yatırım ihtiyaçları doğuruyor.

news.title: First day of Ukraine peace talks 'very productive', US says
news.summary: Delegations from Kyiv, Washington and Moscow are in the United Arab Emirates for the first trilateral talks since February.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: First day of Ukraine peace talks 'very productive', US says
news.summaryTr: Delegations from Kyiv, Washington and Moscow are in the United Arab Emirates for the first trilateral talks since February.
news.articleText: First day of Ukraine peace talks 'very productive', US says - Published The first day of trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine has concluded in Abu Dhabi. While senior officials from Kyiv and Moscow were tight-lipped after the four hour-long discussions - due to resume on Wednesday - US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who did not attend the talks, said they had been "very productive". Although expectations for a breakthrough that ends Russia's full-scale war on Ukraine are low, US officials said earlier that Moscow and Kyiv were privately showing "a little bit of flexibility" on the issue of who would control Ukraine's eastern regions in a postwar scenario. At the start of Tuesday's talks President Donald Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner, told delegates that the US had "narrowed the gaps" between the two sides, without providing details, and hoped to move towards a "solution that hopefully ends the war". Kushner said earlier the talks would be focused on addressing the "postwar security concerns" of both Russia and Ukraine. He and Trump peace envoy Steve Witkoff also met Ukrainian and European and Nato officials on the sidelines of the main meeting. European leaders have largely been excluded from peace talks until now, but they have pushed to be included in the discussions amid concerns that decisions about their continent's security would be made without them. The Americans appear to support this, with Rubio acknowledging during a visit to Paris that the Europeans "are a part of solving this problem for the long term". However, "the Russians have a bad taste in their mouth with the Europeans", according to a US official. Some proposals favoured by EU officials - such as calling an unconditional ceasefire as a prerequisite for peace negotiations - are routinely rejected by Moscow. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said on Tuesday that a truce would just allow Kyiv to regroup. "We will not agree to it," he said. Moscow and Kyiv's positions are still far apart on ending the conflict. A key area of disagreement involves Ukraine's eastern region of Donetsk, which is mostly occupied by Russia. Moscow has demanded that Ukraine relinquish the parts of Donetsk it still holds, while Kyiv wants to freeze the contact line to maintain control over those areas, which it says are crucial to its future security. While neither side has budged on these demands, the US official speaking on the eve of the talks suggested that this was just the public stance and that Moscow and Kyiv had shown "a little bit of flexibility, privately". However, he acknowledged the issue would not be solved without discussions about a new "security architecture". "They will not solve the Donetsk issue and the territorial issue until they know what the security architecture is going to be after the war," the official said. "And keep in mind, we're not going to be able to finalise one without the other." For Ukraine, a post-war "security architecture" may include reassurance that allies will come to its aid if it comes under attack again. For Russia, that could be its longstanding ambition to see Nato roll back from Eastern Europe – which would be alarming to Europeans. The framework being proposed includes security consultations and crisis communications hotlines, as well as "reciprocal de-escalation measures" between the two. The officials also floated the re-activation of the Nato-Russia Council that has been largely paused since 2022. The last round of trilateral talks, held in Geneva in February, ended without a breakthrough. Soon after, the US-Israel war on Iran diverted Washington's attention from Ukraine, and no other discussions were held since. From the start of his second term in office, US President Donald Trump – who once boasted he could end the war in Ukraine within a day – has spearheaded several rounds of talks to end the conflict, albeit with little success. Meanwhile, his increasingly conciliatory approach towards Moscow has fuelled deep unease in Kyiv and across the European Union. After meeting Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev in Washington last week, Trump touted a forthcoming "big, beautiful agreement" on Ukraine that "might involve all of Europe". Many in Ukraine are sceptical that this would result in a fair peace. Ukrainian MP Oleksandr Merezhko, head of the foreign affairs parliamentary committee, told the BBC he believed Trump wanted "a quick deal at the expense of Ukraine", which will certainly be rejected by Kyiv. The only way to make Russia's Vladimir Putin start real negotiations was by putting greater pressure on Russia through sanctions and deep strikes, Merezhko said. "While Putin has a war machine up and running, he has no incentives to negotiate." He also mentioned recent moves by Trump, such as his deal to buy diesel from Russia, as something that "only encourages Moscow to continue the war". Moscow's delegation in Abu Dhabi includes Kremlin aide Vladimir Medinsky, deputy foreign ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, spy chief Igor Kostyukov and army general Yury Zhigarlovsky. Kyiv has sent several senior officials who have been part of previous negotiating teams, including Foreign Intelligence Service head Rustem Umerov, Volodymyr Zelensky's chief of staff Kyrylo Budanov, and MP Davyd Arakhamiya. Away from Abu Dhabi, Russia continues to pummel Ukraine with deadly bombardments and strikes on energy infrastructure, viewed in Kyiv as proof that Moscow wants to corner Ukraine into accepting a deal on Russia's terms. On Monday, Kushner was cautious to point out that the Abu Dhabi talks could at most "build momentum toward the next phase of negotiations". "This is an extraordinarily difficult and complicated conflict," he wrote on X, adding the US was "approaching these discussions with determination and realism." news.title: Arrests made in Mohamed Al Fayed probe in France, police say
news.summary: The Ritz hotel in Paris, which is still owned by the Al Fayed family, is one of the properties searched by police.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Arrests made in Mohamed Al Fayed probe in France, police say
news.summaryTr: The Ritz hotel in Paris, which is still owned by the Al Fayed family, is one of the properties searched by police.
news.articleText: Arrests made in Mohamed Al Fayed probe in France, police say - Published French police have made arrests after three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, were searched in relation to an investigation into Mohamed Al Fayed's abuse. In a confidential letter sent to survivors, the Metropolitan Police confirmed that on 13 and 14 October, French police searched three properties which resulted in a "number of arrests". Met officers were present in what is understood to be a joint operation between British and French authorities. It is the first time any arrests have been made in relation to alleged abuse and trafficking by the former Harrods and Ritz owner. - Mohamed Al Fayed accused of multiple rapes by staff - Published19 September 2024 The Met shared this statement from French authorities with victims: "At this stage of the proceedings, several victims have been interviewed by French investigators, and the investigations are being conducted in liaison with the British authorities. "In this context, searches and evidence-gathering operations were carried out in mid-October 2026, notably within the Hotel Ritz in the 1st arrondissement of Paris, as well as at the Villa Sainte-Thérèse in Saint-Tropez, a former property of Mohamed Al Fayed, and at the Villa Windsor in the 16th arrondissement of Paris, in the presence of British investigators. "Several suspects were taken into police custody, measures which were lifted following their interviews, specifically for the purpose of analyzing digital material seized during the search operations. "The investigations are continuing under the direction of the Paris Public Prosecutor's Office." A Met Police spokesperson confirmed its officers travelled to France in October and were present during the operation. Al Fayed was accused by more than 20 women of sexual assault in a BBC documentary and podcast in September 2024. One of the women featured in the documentary said she was sexually assaulted by Al Fayed at the Ritz hotel in Paris, while another woman said she had been raped by him at the Villa Windsor hotel in Paris. Since those allegations, more than 400 alleged victims or witnesses have come forward to lawyers. The Justice for Fayed and Harrods Survivors group said it welcomed the "significant developments" and cooperation between the Met and French authorities. "We believe that all properties owned by Fayed should be investigated with the same thoroughness as those already searched, wherever they are located, to ensure that no potentially relevant evidence is overlooked," the group said. "We hope these developments represent meaningful progress towards identifying and holding to account all those who facilitated, concealed or assisted his offending, wherever they operated." The survivor advocacy group No One Above said: "France is treating this as organised human trafficking, led by specialists, with properties searched and evidence seized. That is what a serious investigation into a network looks like. "Two years on, survivors are still waiting for the same from the Met. It is time the National Crime Agency took this investigation over." - Published27 September 2024 - Published24 August

The survivor advocacy group No One Above said: "France is treating this as organised human trafficking, led by specialists, with properties searched and evidence seized. That is what a serious investigation into a network looks like. "Two years on, survivors are still waiting for the same from the Met. It is time the National Crime Agency took this investigation over." - Published27 September 2024 - Published24 August

news.summaryTr: ABD'de ekim ayı enflasyonunun beklentileri aşması ve Fed'in faiz artışına yönelik beklentilerin güçlenmesiyle spot altının ons fiyatı TSİ 17.00 itibarıyla yüzde 2'den fazla düşerek 4 bin 55 dolara geriledi.
news.articleText: ABD enflasyonu altını vurdu: Fiyatlar yüzde 2'den fazla geriledi ABD'de ekim ayı enflasyonunun beklentileri aşması ve Fed'in faiz artışına yönelik beklentilerin güçlenmesiyle spot altının ons fiyatı TSİ 17.00 itibarıyla yüzde 2'den fazla düşerek 4 bin 55 dolara geriledi. ABD'de ekim ayı enflasyonunun beklentilerin üzerinde gerçekleşmesi ve Fed'in faiz artışına yönelik beklentilerin güçlenmesiyle altın fiyatları yüzde 2'den fazla geriledi. Spot altının ons fiyatı TSİ 17.00 itibarıyla yüzde 2 düşüşle 4.055 dolar dolara indi. Enflasyon verisinin ardından yatırımcıların Fed'in aralık ayında daha güçlü bir faiz artışına gidebileceği beklentisiyle satışlarını artırdığı belirtildi. ABD'de enflasyon beklentileri aştı ABD Çalışma İstatistikleri Bürosunun (BLS) açıkladığı verilere göre, Tüketici Fiyat Endeksi (TÜFE) ekimde aylık bazda yüzde 0,4 yükseldi. Ekonomistlerin beklentisi yüzde 0,3 artış yönündeydi. Eylülde aylık enflasyon yüzde 0,6 olarak kaydedilmişti. Gıda ve enerji fiyatlarının hariç tutulduğu çekirdek TÜFE ise ekimde yüzde 0,3 arttı. Böylece çekirdek enflasyondaki aylık artış eylül ayındaki seviyesini korurken, piyasa beklentisi yüzde 0,2 düzeyindeydi. Ekim ayı yıllık enflasyonu hesaplanamadı BLS, geçen yıl hükümetin kapanması nedeniyle Ekim 2025 döneminde anket verisi toplayamadığını ve birçok TÜFE endeksi için ilgili ayın verilerini yayımlayamadığını bildirdi. Bu nedenle kurum, Ekim 2026 için bazı endekslerde yıllık değişim oranlarını hesaplayamadı. Altın fiyatları, enflasyon verisi öncesinde de Fed Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi Christopher Waller'ın açıklamalarının etkisiyle baskı altındaydı. Waller, enflasyon görünümünün kötüleşmesi halinde aralık ayında 50 baz puanlık faiz artışının değerlendirilmesi gerektiğini belirtmişti.

news.title: Iran rejects French claims it was behind supermarket fridge hacking
news.summary: Tons of chilled and frozen food was spoiled last month as fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets heated up.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Iran rejects French claims it was behind supermarket fridge hacking
news.summaryTr: Tons of chilled and frozen food was spoiled last month as fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets heated up.
news.articleText: Iran rejects French claims it was behind supermarket fridge hacking - Published Iran has described French accusations that it was behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers as "baseless and hostile". On Monday, the French authorities blamed Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) for the string of hacks, which foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot said were "unprecedented" in terms of their scale and "level of aggression". He added that those responsible would be hit with sanctions. The French cyber-attacks, which led to the destruction of tons of frozen and chilled food, were followed by a similar hacks against supermarkets across several other European countries. It is not known if the instances are linked. Barrot said the attack on France's supermarkets "marks the first large-scale cyber-attack aimed at sabotage on our national territory, and it constitutes a major attack on the nation's interests and the security of the French people". He said the government had summoned the Iranian ambassador to Paris to "lodge a very strong protest against this extremely grave act". France will take "any other necessary and proportionate measures" to respond to the incident and "deter anyone who might seek to repeat it", Barrot added. The Paris prosecutor, Laure Beccuau, said an investigation had been opened into the head of an offensive cyber unit associated with the IRGC as well as his two deputies. Beccuau named the unit as Shahid Kaveh, which she said had an affiliation with the electronic and cyber centre of the IRGC. Shahid Kaveh is the name given to a cluster of hackers thought to be directly employed by the Iranian regime. In recent weeks, a number of commentators and politicians in Iran have argued that the country should extend any retaliation beyond the Middle East if the US and Israel resume the war they started earlier this year. On Monday, some Iranian media outlets denied the French accusations, but there had been no official comment until Tuesday's statement from Iran's foreign ministry. On 11 October, hackers gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units used in many of France's supermarkets. More than 100 of Coopérative U's supermarkets were hit, as well as 180 stores from Intermarché and its Netto brand. In some stores, temperatures of the fridges reportedly rose to 50C (120F) overnight. Other major food retailers including Carrefour, Monoprix and E.Leclerc were also hit by the attack, which targeted software provided by Danish engineering firm Danfoss. The software allows retailers to manage their cold units remotely. Earlier this month a second wave of hacks took place, hitting more than 100 stores across Europe. Supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, while a smaller number of shops were hit in countries including Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland. Separately in August a small number of US military bases had fridges mysteriously malfunction, spoiling food. This incident is also being investigated as deliberate cyber-attacks, Reuters news agency has reported, citing sources familiar with the matter. Since the waves of attacks on freezers, experts have been speculating which hacking groups could be responsible, with Iran being on a list of potential suspects. In spite of a pair of Russian-aligned hacktivist groups claiming they were responsible on Wednesday, few believed them. The French government has not said how it reached the conclusion that Iran was responsible, and attribution of cyber-attacks is extremely hard as hackers are able to hide their locations. Additional reporting by Farshad Bayan, BBC Persian. Related topics - Published2 November

news.title: New regulation for heating oil market, but no price controls
news.summary: The Competition and Markets Authority has investigated the heating oil market in Northern Ireland and other parts of the UK.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: New regulation for heating oil market, but no price controls
news.summaryTr: The Competition and Markets Authority has investigated the heating oil market in Northern Ireland and other parts of the UK.
news.articleText: New regulation for heating oil market, but no price controls - Published Home heating oil suppliers in Northern Ireland will face stricter regulation in the wake of an inquiry by the UK's competition watchdog. However it will not include the sort of price controls applied to the gas and electricity markets. The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) investigated the heating oil market in Northern Ireland and other parts of the UK., external The Economy Minister Caoimhe Archibald said she will now act on the CMA's recommendations. "The CMA identified the need for stronger consumer protection, support for vulnerable households, and more formal dispute resolution arrangements," she told MLAs. She said the changes she was announcing are "proportionate" and will enhance existing heating oil consumer protection "at minimal additional cost". What regulations will be put in place for home heating oil? The measures include a mandatory code of conduct for heating oil suppliers and giving the Consumer Council an enhanced role in helping consumers resolve disputes. The Consumer Council will also lead in the creation of an opt-in register for vulnerable consumers. About two thirds of Northern Ireland households use home heating oil, by far the highest of any UK region. At the start of the US-Israel attack on Iran in March, heating oil prices in Northern Ireland rose by a record monthly rate of 92%. That compared to the previous largest spike of 59% in March 2022, after the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Analysis by the CMA suggested that prices rose even more steeply in Scotland and Wales, where heating oil is typically used in remote rural areas. It found that prices tended to be lower in Northern Ireland overall as it has a competitive range of suppliers and a market which is big enough to minimise delivery costs. The CMA said that the huge spike in prices at the start of the Iran conflict largely reflected rising wholesale costs. It did not recommend price controls suggesting they could be counterproductive. - Published9 September - Published14 September - Published28 September

news.title: Poland’s lower house backs sanctions bill covering crypto freezes
news.summary: The bill is now before the Senate and would broaden the grounds for adding people and companies to Poland’s national sanctions list.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Poland’s lower house backs sanctions bill covering crypto freezes
news.summaryTr: The bill is now before the Senate and would broaden the grounds for adding people and companies to Poland’s national sanctions list.
news.articleText: Poland’s lower house backs sanctions bill covering crypto freezes The bill is now before the Senate and would broaden the grounds for adding people and companies to Poland’s national sanctions list. Poland’s lower house passed a bill that would broaden the country’s sanctions framework and explicitly include crypto assets among the funds authorities can freeze when imposing sanctions. The Sejm approved the government-backed Act on Restrictive Measures on Friday by 240 votes to 202, with one abstention, and forwarded it to the Senate on Monday, according to official parliamentary records. The bill explicitly includes crypto assets, as defined under the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), among financial funds that authorities could freeze when imposing sanctions. Poland’s interior minister would oversee the national sanctions list, with sanctions-listing decisions taking effect the day after authorities publish a designation. Affected individuals and companies could challenge the decision in administrative court, but the bill allows enforcement before a court ruling. Poland already maintains a national sanctions list under a 2022 law aimed at countering support for Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. The bill would expand the grounds for imposing national sanctions to include certain foreign interference and information manipulation that pose a serious threat to national security. The Senate has 30 days to approve, amend or reject the legislation. If it takes no action, Poland’s Constitution treats the bill as approved in the form passed by the Sejm, allowing it to proceed to the president for consideration. Related: US Treasury cuts off MEXC over alleged $16B in illicit transactions

news.title: Civil servant who secretly held five jobs found guilty of fraud
news.summary: Kashim Chowdhury had secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Civil servant who secretly held five jobs found guilty of fraud
news.summaryTr: Kashim Chowdhury had secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries.
news.articleText: Civil servant who secretly held five jobs found guilty of fraud - Published A civil servant who secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries has been found guilty of nine counts of fraud. Kashim Chowdhury, from east London, had five government jobs that overlapped in the spring of 2023. He fraudulently earned more than £284,000 of taxpayers' money. The prosecution accused the 56-year-old of ''deliberate, intentional dishonesty'' and of ''exploiting the system''. After seven hours of deliberation, the jury unanimously found Chowdhury guilty of eight counts of fraud by false representation and one count of fraud by a failure to disclose. The judge said Chowdhury faced a ''very significant custodial sentence''. He added he was refusing bail because of the significance of the crime and for Chowdhury's own wellbeing. 'Abused trust' "This was sustained and deliberate dishonesty," said Sarah Melo, specialist prosecutor at the CPS Serious Economic Organised Crime and International Directorate. "He knew he could not legitimately hold multiple full-time positions at the same time, but continued to conceal what he was doing." A Defra spokesperson said Chowdury "abused the trust placed in him as a public servant", adding that it would use all available avenues to recover the proceeds of Chowdhury's offending. Between 2020 and 2023 Chowdhury had eight full-time public sector roles that overlapped and earned him £350,000 in total. The prosecution told the court that on application forms he provided inaccurate information about his employment status and failed to disclose to government departments that he was already a civil servant. Once he secured the roles he didn't tell his employers he was working elsewhere. He was allowed to work entirely from home because he told his employers he was caring for his mother, whom he lived with in east London. She had dementia and was diagnosed with terminal cancer in 2023. - How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long - Published20 hours ago But rather than reduce his workload to look after her, he kept taking on new jobs. In the spring of 2023, when his mother was a few months away from death, he had jobs at the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, the Department of Health and Social Care, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), the Department for Business and Trade, the Food Standards Agency and the Home Office. During this period he was contracted to work 183 hours a week - more than the number of hours that exist in seven days. Chowdhury said he had taken on so many roles because he feared losing his livelihood after experiencing insecure employment in the past. He was made redundant from a job at the Department for Education in 2013 and was given a diagnosis of PTSD. He said he had not been thinking clearly when applying for jobs ''because of my stress, distress and trauma and due to my panic at the time". But the prosecution barrister, Lucy Organ, told the jury: "He's lied to you in evidence, he's lied to you under oath, which demonstrates the level of deceit he has descended to." A succession of his managers told the court about his poor performance. Especially damning was the evidence given by Dan McCartney who managed Chowdhury at Defra. He said he had to "effectively tell him what to do the whole time". McCartney said that during video calls Chowdhury had his camera switched off blaming technical problems. McCartney said this went on for four to five months. But McCartney said that because Chowdhury was not subject to any formal performance measures at Defra, he was given a permanent job and remained there for two years. The prosecution argued that he used sick notes to cope with his impossible schedule. In March 2023, he was on sick leave from four of the organisations he worked for. But he kept working at the Home Office and did not tell them he was ill. His line manager at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), Aleesha Adams, organised a video call with him in May 2023. By this point he'd been off sick for three months and she wanted to make a plan to get him back to work. She told the jury that at the start of the call he was coughing a lot and waving tissues up to the camera. She also told the jury that he had been wearing white make-up to try to look ill. Adams told the court that as the meeting went on the make-up started coming off his forehead. ''He was sweating, it was like rubbing off so it was darker underneath and darker on the neck." Chowdhury told the jury this was a smear and that he had not been wearing make-up. After the call, Adams discovered that he had logged into the call using a Defra email address. When she challenged him about it he blamed a technical error. Adams grew suspicious. ''I believed he was lying,'' she told the jury. She escalated her concerns up the chain at the UKHSA. But his fraudulent behaviour went on for several more months. The government's National Fraud Initiative flagged suspected fraud to Defra in 2023. Following this, the Defra Investigations Team launched an investigation and as a result, Chowdhury was arrested and interviewed under caution in July 2023. He was dismissed by the civil service in September 2023. Chowdhury has also been accused by his siblings of bullying their mother into increasing his share of the family home days before she died. In a case at the High Court, Chowdhury's two brothers and sister allege that he put "undue influence" on Faijun Nessa to sign documents that meant he would inherit half of her home. The four-storey, six-bedroom home in east London has been valued at £2.1m. His siblings say their mother could not have understood what she was signing because she was "desperately unwell". In January 2023 she was given a terminal diagnosis of stage four metastatic colorectal cancer. The claimants also allege that Mrs Nessa, who was nearly blind and could not speak English, was unaware of what she was signing because the documents were not translated into her native Bengali at the time they were signed. Kashim Chowdhury denies the claims. That case is ongoing. Additional reporting by Ben Sturt.

In the spring of 2023, when his mother was a few months away from death, he had jobs at the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, the Department of Health and Social Care, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), the Department for Business and Trade, the Food Standards Agency and the Home Office. During this period he was contracted to work 183 hours a week - more than the number of hours that exist in seven days. Chowdhury said he had taken on so many roles because he feared losing his livelihood after experiencing insecure employment in the past. He was made redundant from a job at the Department for Education in 2013 and was given a diagnosis of PTSD. He said he had not been thinking clearly when applying for jobs ''because of my stress, distress and trauma and due to my panic at the time". But the prosecution barrister, Lucy Organ, told the jury: "He's lied to you in evidence, he's lied to you under oath, which demonstrates the level of deceit he has descended to." A succession of his managers told the court about his poor performance. Especially damning was the evidence given by Dan McCartney who managed Chowdhury at Defra. He said he had to "effectively tell him what to do the whole time". McCartney said that during video calls Chowdhury had his camera switched off blaming technical problems. McCartney said this went on for four to five months. But McCartney said that because Chowdhury was not subject to any formal performance measures at Defra, he was given a permanent job and remained there for two years. The prosecution argued that he used sick notes to cope with his impossible schedule. In March 2023, he was on sick leave from four of the organisations he worked for. But he kept working at the Home Office and did not tell them he was ill. His line manager at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), Aleesha Adams, organised a video call with him in May 2023. By this point he'd been off sick for three months and she wanted to make a plan to get him back to work. She told the jury that at the start of the call he was coughing a lot and waving tissues up to the camera. She also told the jury that he had been wearing white make-up to try to look ill. Adams told the court that as the meeting went on the make-up started coming off his forehead. ''He was sweating, it was like rubbing off so it was darker underneath and darker on the neck." Chowdhury told the jury this was a smear and that he had not been wearing make-up. After the call, Adams discovered that he had logged into the call using a Defra email address. When she challenged him about it he blamed a technical error. Adams grew suspicious. ''I believed he was lying,'' she told the jury. She escalated her concerns up the chain at the UKHSA. But his fraudulent behaviour went on for several more months. The government's National Fraud Initiative flagged suspected fraud to Defra in 2023. Following this, the Defra Investigations Team launched an investigation and as a result, Chowdhury was arrested and interviewed under caution in July 2023. He was dismissed by the civil service in September 2023. Chowdhury has also been accused by his siblings of bullying their mother into increasing his share of the family home days before she died. In a case at the High Court, Chowdhury's two brothers and sister allege that he put "undue influence" on Faijun Nessa to sign documents that meant he would inherit half of her home. The four-storey, six-bedroom home in east London has been valued at £2.1m. His siblings say their mother could not have understood what she was signing because she was "desperately unwell". In January 2023 she was given a terminal diagnosis of stage four metastatic colorectal cancer. The claimants also allege that Mrs Nessa, who was nearly blind and could not speak English, was unaware of what she was signing because the documents were not translated into her native Bengali at the time they were signed. Kashim Chowdhury denies the claims. That case is ongoing. Additional reporting by Ben Sturt.

news.articleText: İran'dan savaş resti: "ABD ve İsrail'i bekleyen sürprizler var" - İran Genelkurmay Başkanı Tümgeneral Ali Abdullahi, ABD ve İsrail'le olası yeni bir çatışmada "birçok sürprizin ardı ardına ortaya çıkacağını" söyledi. - Abdullahi, İran'ın hedef alınması halinde karşılık vereceklerini belirtti. İran ile ABD ve İsrail arasındaki gerilim sürerken Tahran'dan yeni bir açıklama geldi. İran Genelkurmay Başkanı Tümgeneral Ali Abdullahi, olası bir savaşın yeniden başlaması halinde karşı tarafı bekleyen sürprizler olacağını ifade etti. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle İran resmi haber ajansı IRNA'nın aktardığına göre Abdullahi, Devrim Muhafızları Ordusunun yeni yer altı füze üssünün tanıtım töreninde konuştu. ABD ve İsrail'in tehditlerine değinen Abdullahi, düşmanın askeri gücünün ve sahip olduğu tesislerin İran'ın kararlarını etkilemeyeceğini söyledi. "Gelecekteki savaşta sürprizler olacak" İsrail Başbakanı Binyamin Netanyahu'nun İran'a yönelik açıklamalarına da yanıt veren Abdullahi, Netanyahu'nun "Ya İran'ı yok edeceğiz ya da İran bizi yok edecek" sözlerini hatırlattı. Abdullahi, İran'ın bu tehditlere boyun eğmeyeceğini belirterek, "Onları kesinlikle yok edeceğimiz açıktır" ifadelerini kullandı. İranlı komutan, önceki çatışmalarda ABD ve İsrail'in sahip oldukları askeri imkanları kullandıklarını ancak hedeflerine ulaşamadıklarını öne sürdü. Abdullahi, konuşmasını olası yeni çatışmaya ilişkin şu sözlerle tamamladı: "Gelecekteki savaşta sürprizler ardı ardına ortaya çıkacak."

news.titleTr: Here’s what happened in crypto today
news.summaryTr: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
news.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, Coinbase and Kalshi have joined four other firms backing the CFTC in a lawsuit over whether US exchanges can list perpetual futures tied to individual stocks, cybersecurity firm CertiK urged exchanges to impose hard dollar limits on hot-wallet holdings following the $6.3 billion Binance hack, and blockchain analytics firm Elliptic reported that North Korean hackers used newly created memecoins to launder stolen funds. Coinbase, Kalshi join lawsuit backing CFTC over US stock perp futures Coinbase, Kalshi and four other companies asked a federal court Monday to accept a brief backing the United States Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) in a lawsuit over perpetual futures tied to individual US stocks. According to a proposed amicus brief shared Monday by Coinbase legal representative Molly Abraham, the group also includes Kraken parent Payward, trading companies DRW Holdings and Jump Trading, and crypto investment company Paradigm Operations. The companies argue that stock perpetual futures fall under existing US futures laws. The filing comes days after a federal judge found that the CFTC likely “exceeded its statutory authority” in allowing single-stock perpetuals to trade as security futures. The case could determine whether US exchanges can offer retail traders contracts that track individual stocks without expiring. On Nov. 3, the CFTC announced that single-stock perpetual futures, or stock perps, could begin trading on US-regulated exchanges for the first time. The Capital Markets Alliance Association (CMAA), a newly formed trade and advocacy group representing traditional financial market participants and whose members include Cboe and Citadel Securities, sued the CFTC last week, challenging the CFTC’s authority to allow the contracts to trade. Crypto exchanges need dollar caps on hot wallets, CertiK says Crypto exchanges should impose hard dollar limits on their hot-wallet holdings rather than relying solely on cold-storage ratios to measure security, according to cybersecurity firm CertiK. The recommendation came as several crypto exchanges recently disclosed how much they held in cold wallets, seeking to reassure customers after the record Binance hack that targeted its hot wallets. Crypto exchange Gate reported that 88.26% of its total assets were in cold storage, while Coinbase said it keeps more than 99% of customer assets offline. “Cold storage is a useful measure of online exposure, but it is not a standalone security score,” CertiK’s research team told Cointelegraph. CertiK said crypto exchanges should consider setting hot-wallet caps for each asset and blockchain according to the strictest of three limits: a percentage of customer liabilities, estimated withdrawal needs and an absolute loss ceiling based on the exchange’s financial resources and recovery capabilities. “Flexibility should support operating liquidity, while hard dollar ceilings and circuit breakers limit potential loss,” they said. North Korean hackers create memecoins to launder funds from Binance hack: Elliptic North Korean hackers created memecoins to launder cryptocurrency stolen in the $6.3 billion Binance hack, routing roughly $430,000 through six newly launched tokens on the NEAR blockchain, according to a report from blockchain analytics firm Elliptic. Between Nov. 5 and 7, the hackers created at least six tokens on NEAR and used liquidity pools on decentralized exchanges to move stolen funds between wallets, Elliptic said. The tokens attracted almost no outside trading and were abandoned shortly after launch. The hackers used one set of wallets to swap stolen NEAR tokens for the new memecoins, then used another set to sell those memecoins back into the pools for NEAR. The swaps let them move funds without direct wallet-to-wallet transfers, though the transactions remained traceable onchain. Elliptic said the same laundering technique was also used following the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in 2025, when North Korean-linked actors moved at least $24 million through a newly created token on the TRON blockchain.

news.title: Bitcoin’s ‘best buying opportunity ever’ has arrived: Mark Moss
news.summary: Bitcoin Opportunity Fund co-founder Mark Moss says that with banks and ETFs widening access to Bitcoin he expects a new record high in 2027.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Bitcoin’s ‘best buying opportunity ever’ has arrived: Mark Moss
news.summaryTr: Bitcoin Opportunity Fund co-founder Mark Moss says that with banks and ETFs widening access to Bitcoin he expects a new record high in 2027.
news.articleText: Bitcoin’s ‘best buying opportunity ever’ has arrived: Mark Moss Bitcoin Opportunity Fund co-founder Mark Moss says that with banks and ETFs widening access to Bitcoin he expects a new record high in 2027. Wall Street’s embrace of Bitcoin has created the “best buying opportunity ever,” according to investor Mark Moss. Moss co-founded the Bitcoin Opportunity Fund, where he is an advisory partner. In 2025, UK-listed Satsuma Technology appointed him chief Bitcoin strategist. Moss tells Cointelegraph on the latest episode of Trade Secrets that he first bought Bitcoin in 2015 at about $300, during a recovery from a $1,000 to $200 plunge. “It was so risky,” Moss recalls of buying back then. In contrast, today, “you have consensus from the US government and Wall Street.” “But most people still think it’s a scam,” he says. That skepticism opens buying opportunities as Bitcoin starts to cross what Moss calls the “chasm” between early adopters and mainstream investors. Banks and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have made Bitcoin easier to buy and financial advisers could help persuade clients who have stayed away previously to consider investing. Related: Strategy shareholders approve daily dividends for four preferred stocks Moss calls bottom but Bitcoin keeps falling Bitcoin briefly climbed above $80,000 after the Democrats took control of the US Congress in the midterm elections, then gave back those gains as tech stocks sold off. By Friday, it fell to $74,762, its lowest level since August and remains in the doldrums at the time of writing. Despite the selloff, Moss points to the reaction to the $6.3 billion Binance hack as a sign that sellers were running out. “The price didn’t really drop,” he says. Bitcoin fell to $76,320 after the breach and slid to $74,762 on Friday, erasing its post-election gains. It fell further to about $73,500 late Sunday, its lowest level since August, after Nvidia’s board announced it would investigate reports that CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. Bitcoin found another bottom after reports of Nvidia CEO’s scandal. Source: CoinMarketCap Flows into US spot Bitcoin ETFs swung sharply during election week. The funds took in about $75 million on Wednesday, then shed $430 million on Thursday. History is on the side of hodlers however. Bitcoin gained an average of about 53% in the 12 months after previous US midterms, Moss says, using data going back to 2014. That leaves three completed election cycles in his sample. He says he expects Bitcoin to set a new all-time high in 2027. Moss backs Strategy but would keep his Bitcoin Moss thinks the Bitcoin treasury company to own is Strategy (MSTR), but believes that holding Bitcoin yourself is still superior. Strategy began buying Bitcoin in 2020 and turned those purchases into a core part of its business. It has used stock and debt sales to fund its purchases, giving investors a way to bet on Bitcoin through a publicly traded company. By Nov. 2, Strategy held 849,327 BTC, more than 4% of Bitcoin’s maximum supply. “I don’t think there’s another publicly traded company that will outperform Strategy over the next ten years,” Moss says. Strategy has the world’s largest corporate Bitcoin trove. Source: BitcoinTreasuries.Net Leverage can help a Bitcoin treasury company’s shares outperform the cryptocurrency it holds when its price rises. But even if Strategy outperforms, Moss wouldn’t trade his Bitcoin holdings for its shares. Related: 1inch lawyer sees agencies driving US crypto regulation as midterms unfold Before Moss bought his first Bitcoin, he made a living buying foreclosed properties, fixing them up and selling them. He moved into property development, then built and sold a medical equipment business. He says he put the proceeds into Southern California real estate. When the market crashed in 2008, he lost it all. “The reward of being right is not worth the risk of getting it wrong,” he says. Even with his outlook for Strategy, Moss says he’d keep his Bitcoin and use only a small share of his portfolio to pursue higher returns through treasury stocks. A journey of $1 million Bitcoin starts with small allocations In Moss’s model, Bitcoin could reach $1 million under certain circumstances, when it competes with stocks, bonds, gold and real estate for a considerable share of investors’ wealth. The model estimates how much those assets are worth, projects how that pool could grow as the global money supply expands and calculates a Bitcoin price based on the share it captures. Financial advisers could help bring in that money via one client’s portfolio at a time, encouraging them to shift a few percentage points out of stocks or bonds and into Bitcoin. The scenario depends on a critical mass of clients doing that, to the point where all those small allocations add up. The model also assumes Bitcoin stays secure and decentralized. Asked what could derail the scenario, Moss pointed to a failure that compromised either feature. Moss says $1 million is possible by 2030... though hodler’s might have to wait until 2032. news.titleTr: French wartime resistance heroine Solange Alexandre dies aged 104
news.summaryTr: With 30 men under her orders, she organised sabotage operations, sheltered Allied airmen and joined the fight against the occupying German forces.
news.articleText: French wartime resistance heroine Solange Alexandre dies aged 104 - Published One of France's last Resistance heroes from World War Two has died at the age of 104. Solange Alexandre was also a rare woman who, with her future husband, created and commanded her own unit of anti-German fighters. After serving as a Resistance courier from 1941, three years later she founded the Pas-de-Boeuf network near the town of Ruillé-sur-Loir. With some 30 men under her orders, she organised sabotage operations, sheltered Allied airmen and, after the Allied landings in Normandy on D-Day in 1944, joined the fight against the occupying German forces. President Emmanuel Macron was among many to pay tribute to Alexandre, after her death was announced at a nursing home in Le Mans. "She said she only ever did her duty. But her duty was our freedom. France will never forget. Thank you," Macron posted on social media. Born in 1922 in the Sarthe department of western France, Solange Alexandre, née Dubuisson, grew up in a patriotic family that had suffered in World War One. "My mother lost her first husband in the war, and my father was wounded in 1917. The words homeland and honour were very important to us. They were in my blood," she recalled in her memoirs. In June 1940 she heard on the radio the appeal from General Charles de Gaulle in London, calling on the French not to give up the struggle against Germany. She had never heard of him, but that did not matter. "From that moment I knew I had to join up," she wrote. Some months later she was recruited by a friend of her father's – a Tunisian-born French army veteran called Saïd Belhaffaf, who had joined the Resistance. Using the code-name Corlay, she criss-crossed the region around Le Mans by bicycle, gathering information and passing on messages. news.title: California police investigate after 27 fall ill at half-marathon running event
news.summary: A local hospital says runners had "unusual" symptoms after racing on an atypically hot day.

news.titleTr: California police investigate after 27 fall ill at half-marathon running event
news.summaryTr: A local hospital says runners had "unusual" symptoms after racing on an atypically hot day.
news.articleText: California police investigate after 27 fall ill at half-marathon running event - Published Police in Santa Barbara, California, are investigating after nearly 30 people had to seek medical care at a half-marathon running event held in the city on Sunday. In a statement provided to the BBC's US partner CBS News, officers said they received a report from Santa Barbara Cottage Hospital about race participants who sought medical treatment "for unusual symptoms" after the race ended. "The cause of the reported symptoms has not been confirmed," the statement added. Cottage Health, which operates the hospital, told CBS it had seen "a larger than expected number of emergency visits" from those who ran the race. "There is no specific action recommended for the public at this time; however, participants who feel unwell should seek medical attention and follow guidance from healthcare professionals," police said. Cottage Hospital said it treated 27 people from the half marathon at emergency rooms in Santa Barbara and the nearby city of Goleta. The vast majority of them - 24 - were discharged after treatment, while three people were still in hospital as of Monday in stable condition. Several thousand people ran the half marathon on a hotter-than-usual day in Santa Barbara along the Pacific Ocean. Temperatures reportedly reached 86F (27C) by midday, compared to a typical early November temperature of low 70s. One of the runners who went to hospital told local news outlet KEYT-TV that they had lost consciousness and could not remember parts of the race. "It is awfully suspicious," said the runner, who declined to be identified. "We had people saying they were hallucinating." "I am not too familiar with heat exhaustion but I have never seen anyone not remembering a long portion of their run," the runner added. Event director David Monico told US media that 15 people were taken from the medical tent to local hospitals because of dehydration and overheating. The BBC has contacted the Santa Barbara Police Department, Cottage Health and the half marathon organisers for further comment. Related topics - Published6 days ago - Published6 days ago

news.titleTr: Türk iş insanından siber saldırı uyarısı: İngiltere'de 158 yıllık şirket iflas etti
news.summaryTr: Avrupalı Türk Markalar Birliği Başkanı Vehbi Keleş, kendi şirketinin de siber saldırıya uğradığını açıklayarak işletmeleri uyardı. İngiltere'de 158 yıllık, 700 çalışanlı bir şirketin siber saldırı sonrası iflas ettiğini belirten Keleş, alınması gereken önlemleri anlattı.
news.articleText: Türk iş insanından siber saldırı uyarısı: İngiltere'de 158 yıllık şirket iflas etti - Avrupalı Türk Markalar Birliği Başkanı Vehbi Keleş, kendi şirketinin de siber saldırıya uğradığını açıklayarak işletmeleri uyardı. İngiltere'de 158 yıllık, 700 çalışanlı bir şirketin siber saldırı sonrası iflas ettiğini belirten Keleş, alınması gereken önlemleri anlattı. Avrupalı Türk Markalar Birliği (ATMB) Başkanı Vehbi Keleş, CNBC-e Londra Temsilcisi Berfu Güven'in canlı yayında yönelttiği soruları yanıtladı. İngiltere'deki Türk markalarının 2026 yılındaki performansını değerlendiren Keleş, artan enerji ve nakliye maliyetleri, tüketicilerin stok yapma eğilimi, siber saldırılar ve Türkiye ile İngiltere arasındaki ticari ilişkiler hakkında açıklamalarda bulundu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Enerji maliyetlerindeki artışın önce nakliyeye, ardından üretime ve diğer alanlara yansıdığını belirten Keleş, Türk markalarını en fazla zorlayan unsurun nakliye maliyetleri olduğunu söyledi. Nakliye giderlerinin petrol fiyatlarına bağlı olduğunu ifade eden Keleş, Kızıldeniz'de yaşanan sorunlar nedeniyle sevkiyat sürelerinin de uzayabildiğini kaydetti. Türkiye dahil 36 ülkeden ürün getirerek İngiltere pazarında satışa sunduklarını belirten Keleş, tüketicilerin evde stok yapmaya yönelik çağrılarının satışlara etkisini de değerlendirdi. Makarna, bakliyat ve konserve satışlarında yüzde 40'a varan artış İngiltere'de stok yapma çağrılarının ardından bazı ürün gruplarında satışların arttığını belirten Keleş, ancak pandemi dönemindekine benzer bir kaos yaşanmadığını söyledi. Makarna, bakliyat ve konserve gibi ürünlerin satışlarında yüzde 20 ile yüzde 40 arasında artış görüldüğünü ifade eden Keleş, bunun tüketimin aynı oranda arttığı anlamına gelmediğini vurguladı. Satın alınan ürünlerin evlerde bekletildiğini belirten Keleş, öne çekilen alışverişlerin ilerleyen dönemlerde satışların yavaşlamasına neden olabileceğini söyledi. Pandemi döneminin şirketler açısından önemli bir tecrübe olduğunu ifade eden Keleş, Türk markalarının mevcut sürece hazırlıklı olduğunu dile getirdi. "Siber saldırıyı ben yaşadım" Avrupa'da yaşanan siber saldırıların şu aşamada Türk markaları açısından bir sorun oluşturmadığını belirten Keleş, kendi şirketinin de geçen yıl siber saldırıya uğradığını açıkladı. Saldırının ardından şirketin sistemlerine erişilemediğini anlatan Keleş, müşteri listeleri ve adresler dahil birçok veriye ulaşılamadığını söyledi. Yedekleme sisteminin de saldırıdan etkilendiğini belirten Keleş, çalışanlarına her akşam USB belleklere manuel yedek almalarını söylediğini ifade etti. Bu yedekler sayesinde ertesi gün sistemleri yeniden kurabildiklerini aktaran Keleş, şirketin veri kaybı yaşamadan faaliyetlerine devam ettiğini belirtti. Saldırı sonrasında yeni sunucular ve güvenlik duvarları için 30-40 bin civarında bir maliyet oluştuğunu söyleyen Keleş, asıl büyük riskin şirketin tamamen kaybedilmesi olduğunu vurguladı. İngiltere'de yaklaşık 158 yıllık geçmişe ve 700 çalışana sahip bir nakliye şirketinin siber saldırı sonrasında iflas ettiğini belirten Keleş, manuel yedekleme sistemleri bulunmasaydı kendi şirketlerinin de çok büyük maliyetlerle karşılaşabileceğini söyledi. "Bana olmaz demeyin" uyarısı İnternete bağlı her sistemin siber saldırılara açık olduğunu belirten Keleş, şirketleri güvenlik önlemleri konusunda uyardı. Özellikle soğuk hava depolarında kullanılan cihazların fabrika çıkış şifrelerinin değiştirilmesi gerektiğini söyleyen Keleş, bu cihazlar için yeni ve güvenli şifreler oluşturulmasının önemine dikkat çekti. Fransa'da yaşanan bir siber saldırının ardından İngiltere'deki üç soğuk hava deposunun da saldırıya uğradığını belirten Keleş, kendi şirketlerine yönelik saldırının Ukrayna üzerinden geldiğini ancak bunun saldırıyı gerçekleştiren kişinin Ukraynalı olduğu anlamına gelmediğini ifade etti. Stok çağrıları raf fiyatlarına yansımadı Stok yapma çağrılarının ve şirketlerin aldığı ek tedbirlerin şu aşamada raf fiyatlarına yansımadığını belirten Keleş, tüketicilerin paniğe kapılmasına gerek olmadığını söyledi. Keleş, sürecin normal seyrinde devam etmesi halinde ilave maliyetlerin de raf fiyatlarına yansımayabileceğini ifade etti. Türkiye ile İngiltere arasındaki yeni anlaşma için 2027 beklentisi Türkiye ile İngiltere arasında müzakere edilen yeni serbest ticaret anlaşmasına ilişkin de değerlendirmelerde bulunan Keleş, imza takviminin henüz netleşmediğini söyledi. Anlaşmanın büyük ihtimalle 2027 yılının ilk altı ayında imzalanmasını beklediklerini belirten Keleş, iki ülke arasındaki dış ticaret verilerini de paylaştı. Ekim sonu itibarıyla Türkiye'nin İngiltere'ye ihracatında yüzde 2,2 düşüş görüldüğünü ifade eden Keleş, Birleşik Krallık'ın Türkiye'ye ihracatında ise yüzde 2,9 artış yaşandığını belirtti. Sektörel verilere de değinen Keleş, Türkiye'nin İngiltere'ye ihracatında gıdada yüzde 3, hazır giyimde yüzde 7 ve mobilyada yüzde 2 düşüş görüldüğünü söyledi. Otomotiv sektöründe de gerileme yaşandığını ifade etti. Buna karşılık elektrik ve elektronik sektöründe yüzde 11, çelik sektöründe ise yaklaşık yüzde 60 artış kaydedildiğini belirtti. Türk markaları İngiliz marketlerinde neden etnik ürün raflarında kalıyor? Yaklaşık 20 yıldır İngiltere'deki zincir marketlere ürün verdiklerini belirten Keleş, Türk markalarının bu pazarda karşılaştığı sorunlara da değindi. Türkiye'nin küresel ölçekte tanınan bir markasının bulunmamasının zincir marketlerdeki konumlarını etkilediğini söyleyen Keleş, Türk ürünlerinin çoğunlukla etnik ürün raflarında yer aldığını ifade etti. Türkiye'de çok büyük olan bir markanın İngiliz market zincirleri açısından daha önce hiç karşılaşılmamış bir ürün olabileceğini belirten Keleş, markaların uluslararası pazarlarda tanınması için küreselleşmeye ve marka yatırımlarına önem verilmesi gerektiğini söyledi. 2027'de fiyatlar düşebilir İngiltere'deki Türk markalarının 2027 yılına ilişkin beklentilerini de paylaşan Keleş, mevcut sorunların çözülmesi halinde fiyatların yeniden düşmeye başlayabileceğini ifade etti. Keleş, 2027 yılının herkesin güzel ticaret yaptığı önemli bir yıl olmasını umut ettiklerini söyledi.

Türkiye'nin küresel ölçekte tanınan bir markasının bulunmamasının zincir marketlerdeki konumlarını etkilediğini söyleyen Keleş, Türk ürünlerinin çoğunlukla etnik ürün raflarında yer aldığını ifade etti. Türkiye'de çok büyük olan bir markanın İngiliz market zincirleri açısından daha önce hiç karşılaşılmamış bir ürün olabileceğini belirten Keleş, markaların uluslararası pazarlarda tanınması için küreselleşmeye ve marka yatırımlarına önem verilmesi gerektiğini söyledi. 2027'de fiyatlar düşebilir İngiltere'deki Türk markalarının 2027 yılına ilişkin beklentilerini de paylaşan Keleş, mevcut sorunların çözülmesi halinde fiyatların yeniden düşmeye başlayabileceğini ifade etti. Keleş, 2027 yılının herkesin güzel ticaret yaptığı önemli bir yıl olmasını umut ettiklerini söyledi.

news.titleTr: Piyasaların odağındaki veri açıklandı: ABD'de enflasyon beklentileri aştı
news.summaryTr: ABD'de Tüketici Fiyat Endeksi (TÜFE), ekimde aylık yüzde 0,4 arttı. Böylece aylık enflasyon eylüldeki yüzde 0,6 seviyesinden gerilerken, gıda ve enerji hariç çekirdek TÜFE yüzde 0,3 yükseldi.
news.articleText: Piyasaların odağındaki veri açıklandı: ABD'de enflasyon beklentileri aştı ABD'de Tüketici Fiyat Endeksi (TÜFE), ekimde aylık yüzde 0,4 arttı. Böylece aylık enflasyon eylüldeki yüzde 0,6 seviyesinden gerilerken, gıda ve enerji hariç çekirdek TÜFE yüzde 0,3 yükseldi. ABD Çalışma İstatistikleri Bürosu, ağustos ayına ilişkin tüketici fiyat endeksi verilerini açıkladı. ABD'de enflasyon beklentileri aştı ABD'de tüketicilerin kısa, orta ve uzun vadeli enflasyon beklentileri Ekim ayında değişmeyerek sırasıyla yüzde 3,9, yüzde 3,3 ve yüzde 3 seviyelerinde kalmıştı. Açıklanan verilere göre ABD'de Tüketici Fiyat Endeksi (TÜFE), ekim ayında aylık bazda yüzde 0,4 artarak eylüldeki yüzde 0,6'lık yükselişin altında gerçekleşti. ABD Çalışma İstatistikleri Bürosu (BLS), Ekim 2026 dönemine ilişkin tüketici fiyat endeksi verilerini açıkladı. Buna göre, Tüketici Fiyat Endeksi ekimde mevsim etkilerinden arındırılmış olarak aylık bazda yüzde 0,4 arttı. Endeks, eylül ayında yüzde 0,6 yükselmişti. Barınma endeksi ekimde yüzde 0,3 artarken, bu kalem aylık enflasyondaki toplam yükselişin yüzde 30'undan fazlasını oluşturdu. Gıda endeksi aynı dönemde yüzde 0,5 artış kaydetti. Evde tüketilen gıda fiyatları yüzde 0,4, dışarıda tüketilen gıda fiyatları ise yüzde 0,5 yükseldi. Enerji endeksi de ekimde yüzde 0,7 arttı. Söz konusu endekste eylül ayında yüzde 5,2'lik artış yaşanmıştı. Çekirdek enflasyon yüzde 0,3 arttı Gıda ve enerji kalemlerinin hariç tutulduğu çekirdek TÜFE, ekimde aylık bazda yüzde 0,3 yükseldi. Çekirdek enflasyondaki artış ağustos ve eylül aylarında da yüzde 0,3 olarak kaydedilmişti. Ekim ayında eğlence, sağlık hizmetleri, motorlu taşıt sigortası, ev eşyaları ve hizmetleri ile eğitim kalemlerinde fiyat artışları görüldü. Buna karşılık, kullanılmış otomobil ve kamyon fiyatları ile iletişim endeksinde düşüş kaydedildi.

news.title: Bitcoin may benefit as global tightening slows, Binance Research says
news.summary: Binance Research says Bitcoin could find support as global monetary tightening slows, even as markets price in a December Fed rate hike.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Bitcoin may benefit as global tightening slows, Binance Research says
news.summaryTr: Binance Research says Bitcoin could find support as global monetary tightening slows, even as markets price in a December Fed rate hike.
news.articleText: Bitcoin may benefit as global tightening slows, Binance Research says Binance Research says Bitcoin could find support as global monetary tightening slows, even as markets price in a December Fed rate hike. Bitcoin could find support before major central banks start cutting rates if the spread of rate hikes continues to slow, Binance Research said Tuesday. Eight of the 10 central banks Binance tracks had raised rates over the last six months, including Sweden’s announced increase on Nov. 4, with the momentum of tightening starting to ease since its July peak, Binance Research said in a Tuesday report shared with Cointelegraph. “Whether this easing continues into early 2027 will be key to judging whether the macro backdrop is turning less hostile for crypto,” the report said. Binance pointed to the previous cycle. Bitcoin (BTC) bottomed in November 2022, and its six-month return turned positive in February 2023, before any of the central banks in the index began cutting rates. Pace of G10 banks tightening and Bitcoin’s 6-month returns. Source: Binance Research Similarly, in 2024, monetary tightening measures led to Bitcoin delivering its “strongest” six-month return of the cycle, exceeding 160% in March, Binance said. “In each case, BTC moved with the direction of global policy, not its level,” the report adds. Related: Analysts see no broader ‘contagion’ from $6.3B Binance hack December rate hike odds mount following Waller’s speech A US rate increase remains in play. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said Tuesday he was leaning toward a quarter-point hike in December and would consider a half-point move if core inflation remained elevated. Odds of a 25-basis-point hike in December rose from 76.3% to 96.3% on Tuesday, according to CME Group’s FedWatch Tool. In a Nov. 2 report, Bitwise also argued that a slowdown in economic growth expectations could eventually prompt central banks to pivot towards easing monetary policy, potentially creating a more favourable environment for Bitcoin. BTC/USD, 1-year chart. Source: CoinMarketCap Bitcoin’s price fell 3.5% during the past week, extending its one-year decline to 30%. The world’s first cryptocurrency was trading at $74,131, or 41% below its $126,198 all-time high, according to CoinMarketCap. Magazine: Wall Street killed Bitcoin’s wild rallies: 10x’s Markus Thielen

news.title: Goldman Sachs CEO'su açıkladı: Yapay zekaya milyarlarca dolarlık talep sürüyor
news.summary: Goldman Sachs CEO'su David Solomon, yapay zeka altyapısına yönelik yatırımların geri dönüşüne ilişkin soru işaretlerine rağmen finansman talebinin güçlü seyrettiğini söyledi. Solomon, yapay zekanın uzun vadede ekonomide verimliliği artıracağına inandığını vurguladı.

news.titleTr: Goldman Sachs CEO'su açıkladı: Yapay zekaya milyarlarca dolarlık talep sürüyor
news.summaryTr: Goldman Sachs CEO'su David Solomon, yapay zeka altyapısına yönelik yatırımların geri dönüşüne ilişkin soru işaretlerine rağmen finansman talebinin güçlü seyrettiğini söyledi. Solomon, yapay zekanın uzun vadede ekonomide verimliliği artıracağına inandığını vurguladı.
news.articleText: Goldman Sachs CEO'su açıkladı: Yapay zekaya milyarlarca dolarlık talep sürüyor - Goldman Sachs CEO'su David Solomon, yapay zeka altyapısına yönelik yatırımların geri dönüşüne ilişkin soru işaretlerine rağmen finansman talebinin güçlü seyrettiğini söyledi. Goldman Sachs Üst Yöneticisi (CEO) David Solomon, yapay zeka sektöründeki yatırım iştahının sürdüğünü belirtti. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle CNBC'ye konuşan Solomon, yatırımcıların altyapı harcamalarının geri dönüşünü yeniden değerlendirdiği bir dönemde, yapay zeka sermaye piyasası işlemlerinde son haftalarda oldukça aktif olduklarını söyledi. Solomon, yapay zeka altyapısının kurulmasına ve teknolojinin büyümesini destekleyen yatırımlara yönelik talebin güçlü kalmaya devam ettiğini ifade etti. Yapay zeka hisselerinde satış baskısı Solomon, siyasi ortamda yaşanan değişimlerin piyasada yeniden ayarlamalara ve dalgalanmalara yol açabileceğini belirtti. Buna karşın yapay zekanın ekonomide verimliliği artırma potansiyeline ilişkin uzun vadeli iyimserliğini koruduğunu dile getirdi. Çip üreticileri ve yeni nesil bulut hizmeti sağlayıcıları dahil olmak üzere yapay zeka bağlantılı hisseler, son haftalarda sert satışlarla karşılaştı. Yatırımcılar, sektöre aktarılan yüz milyarlarca dolarlık sermayenin yeterli getiri sağlayıp sağlamayacağını sorgulamaya başladı. ABD ara seçimleri öncesinde başlayan satış baskısı, Demokratların seçimlerde elde ettiği sonuçların ardından sektör üzerindeki siyasi baskının artabileceği endişesiyle derinleşti. Anthropic'in halka arz süreci yakından izleniyor Piyasa algısındaki değişim, halka arza hazırlanan yapay zeka şirketi Anthropic açısından da önemli bir döneme denk geldi. Goldman Sachs, şirketin halka arz sürecine liderlik eden bankalar arasında bulunuyor. Yapay zeka yatırımlarında veri merkezleri, çipler, enerji altyapısı ve bulut hizmetleri için yapılan harcamalar öne çıkıyor. Yatırımcıların odağında ise bu yüksek maliyetli yatırımların ne zaman ve hangi ölçüde gelir ve kâra dönüşeceği bulunuyor.

İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığınca sermaye piyasalarında gerçekleştirilen işlemlere ilişkin fon soruşturması devam ediyor. Soruşturma kapsamında gözaltına alınan OMG Capital Advisors Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Ömer Murat Gülkan, eski Takasbank Genel Müdürü Yunus Arıncı, Bulls Yatırım Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Kemal Akkaya, Ruzy Madencilik Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Nureddin Çevik ve Lydia Holding Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Enver Çevik'in emniyetteki işlemleri tamamlandı. Sağlık kontrolünün ardından Çağlayan'daki İstanbul Adliyesi'ne getirilen şüphelilerin savcılıktaki işlemleri sürüyor.

Moskova'daki Taganskiy Bölge Mahkemesi, ülkede yasaklı kabul edilen içerikleri kaldırmadıkları gerekçesiyle Apple, Google, Telegram ve Wikipedia'nın işletmecisi Wikimedia Vakfına para cezası uygulanmasına karar verdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Mahkemenin kararına göre Wikimedia Vakfı 15,2 milyon ruble, Google ve Telegram ayrı ayrı 3,8 milyon ruble, Apple ise 3,5 milyon ruble ceza ödeyecek. Telegram'a yönelik suçlama dikkat çekti Şirketlere verilen cezaların gerekçesi, Rusya'da yasaklı içeriklerin kaldırılmaması ve ilgili yasal yükümlülüklerin yerine getirilmemesi olarak açıklandı. Telegram'a yönelik davanın, Rusya Silahlı Kuvvetleri hakkında yanlış bilgi içerdiği belirtilen paylaşımlarla ilgili olduğu bildirildi. Apple hakkındaki duruşmanın ise şirketin gizli bilgilerinin paylaşılabileceği gerekçesiyle basına kapalı gerçekleştirildiği aktarıldı. Rusya, daha önce de yasaklı içerikleri kaldırmadıkları veya ülkedeki yasal düzenlemelere uymadıkları gerekçesiyle teknoloji şirketlerine para cezaları uygulamıştı. Bu yaptırımlar, ülkede faaliyet gösteren küresel dijital platformlarla Rus makamları arasındaki hukuki anlaşmazlıkların bir parçası olarak öne çıkıyor.
