items.title: Civil servant who secretly held five jobs found guilty of fraud
items.summary: Kashim Chowdhury had secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Civil servant who secretly held five jobs found guilty of fraud
items.summaryTr: Kashim Chowdhury had secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries.
items.articleText: Civil servant who secretly held five jobs found guilty of fraud - Published A civil servant who secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries has been found guilty of nine counts of fraud. Kashim Chowdhury, from east London, had five government jobs that overlapped in the spring of 2023. He fraudulently earned more than £284,000 of taxpayers' money. The prosecution accused the 56-year-old of ''deliberate, intentional dishonesty'' and of ''exploiting the system''. After seven hours of deliberation, the jury unanimously found Chowdhury guilty of eight counts of fraud by false representation and one count of fraud by a failure to disclose. The judge said Chowdhury faced a ''very significant custodial sentence''. He added he was refusing bail because of the significance of the crime and for Chowdhury's own wellbeing. 'Abused trust' "This was sustained and deliberate dishonesty," said Sarah Melo, specialist prosecutor at the CPS Serious Economic Organised Crime and International Directorate. "He knew he could not legitimately hold multiple full-time positions at the same time, but continued to conceal what he was doing." A Defra spokesperson said Chowdury "abused the trust placed in him as a public servant", adding that it would use all available avenues to recover the proceeds of Chowdhury's offending. Between 2020 and 2023 Chowdhury had eight full-time public sector roles that overlapped and earned him £350,000 in total. The prosecution told the court that on application forms he provided inaccurate information about his employment status and failed to disclose to government departments that he was already a civil servant. Once he secured the roles he didn't tell his employers he was working elsewhere. He was allowed to work entirely from home because he told his employers he was caring for his mother, whom he lived with in east London. She had dementia and was diagnosed with terminal cancer in 2023. - How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long - Published20 hours ago But rather than reduce his workload to look after her, he kept taking on new jobs. In the spring of 2023, when his mother was a few months away from death, he had jobs at the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, the Department of Health and Social Care, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), the Department for Business and Trade, the Food Standards Agency and the Home Office. During this period he was contracted to work 183 hours a week - more than the number of hours that exist in seven days. Chowdhury said he had taken on so many roles because he feared losing his livelihood after experiencing insecure employment in the past. He was made redundant from a job at the Department for Education in 2013 and was given a diagnosis of PTSD. He said he had not been thinking clearly when applying for jobs ''because of my stress, distress and trauma and due to my panic at the time". But the prosecution barrister, Lucy Organ, told the jury: "He's lied to you in evidence, he's lied to you under oath, which demonstrates the level of deceit he has descended to." A succession of his managers told the court about his poor performance. Especially damning was the evidence given by Dan McCartney who managed Chowdhury at Defra. He said he had to "effectively tell him what to do the whole time". McCartney said that during video calls Chowdhury had his camera switched off blaming technical problems. McCartney said this went on for four to five months. But McCartney said that because Chowdhury was not subject to any formal performance measures at Defra, he was given a permanent job and remained there for two years. The prosecution argued that he used sick notes to cope with his impossible schedule. In March 2023, he was on sick leave from four of the organisations he worked for. But he kept working at the Home Office and did not tell them he was ill. His line manager at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), Aleesha Adams, organised a video call with him in May 2023. By this point he'd been off sick for three months and she wanted to make a plan to get him back to work. She told the jury that at the start of the call he was coughing a lot and waving tissues up to the camera. She also told the jury that he had been wearing white make-up to try to look ill. Adams told the court that as the meeting went on the make-up started coming off his forehead. ''He was sweating, it was like rubbing off so it was darker underneath and darker on the neck." Chowdhury told the jury this was a smear and that he had not been wearing make-up. After the call, Adams discovered that he had logged into the call using a Defra email address. When she challenged him about it he blamed a technical error. Adams grew suspicious. ''I believed he was lying,'' she told the jury. She escalated her concerns up the chain at the UKHSA. But his fraudulent behaviour went on for several more months. The government's National Fraud Initiative flagged suspected fraud to Defra in 2023. Following this, the Defra Investigations Team launched an investigation and as a result, Chowdhury was arrested and interviewed under caution in July 2023. He was dismissed by the civil service in September 2023. Chowdhury has also been accused by his siblings of bullying their mother into increasing his share of the family home days before she died. In a case at the High Court, Chowdhury's two brothers and sister allege that he put "undue influence" on Faijun Nessa to sign documents that meant he would inherit half of her home. The four-storey, six-bedroom home in east London has been valued at £2.1m. His siblings say their mother could not have understood what she was signing because she was "desperately unwell". In January 2023 she was given a terminal diagnosis of stage four metastatic colorectal cancer. The claimants also allege that Mrs Nessa, who was nearly blind and could not speak English, was unaware of what she was signing because the documents were not translated into her native Bengali at the time they were signed. Kashim Chowdhury denies the claims. That case is ongoing. Additional reporting by Ben Sturt.

But the prosecution barrister, Lucy Organ, told the jury: "He's lied to you in evidence, he's lied to you under oath, which demonstrates the level of deceit he has descended to." A succession of his managers told the court about his poor performance. Especially damning was the evidence given by Dan McCartney who managed Chowdhury at Defra. He said he had to "effectively tell him what to do the whole time". McCartney said that during video calls Chowdhury had his camera switched off blaming technical problems. McCartney said this went on for four to five months. But McCartney said that because Chowdhury was not subject to any formal performance measures at Defra, he was given a permanent job and remained there for two years. The prosecution argued that he used sick notes to cope with his impossible schedule. In March 2023, he was on sick leave from four of the organisations he worked for. But he kept working at the Home Office and did not tell them he was ill. His line manager at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), Aleesha Adams, organised a video call with him in May 2023. By this point he'd been off sick for three months and she wanted to make a plan to get him back to work. She told the jury that at the start of the call he was coughing a lot and waving tissues up to the camera. She also told the jury that he had been wearing white make-up to try to look ill. Adams told the court that as the meeting went on the make-up started coming off his forehead. ''He was sweating, it was like rubbing off so it was darker underneath and darker on the neck." Chowdhury told the jury this was a smear and that he had not been wearing make-up. After the call, Adams discovered that he had logged into the call using a Defra email address. When she challenged him about it he blamed a technical error. Adams grew suspicious. ''I believed he was lying,'' she told the jury. She escalated her concerns up the chain at the UKHSA. But his fraudulent behaviour went on for several more months. The government's National Fraud Initiative flagged suspected fraud to Defra in 2023. Following this, the Defra Investigations Team launched an investigation and as a result, Chowdhury was arrested and interviewed under caution in July 2023. He was dismissed by the civil service in September 2023. Chowdhury has also been accused by his siblings of bullying their mother into increasing his share of the family home days before she died. In a case at the High Court, Chowdhury's two brothers and sister allege that he put "undue influence" on Faijun Nessa to sign documents that meant he would inherit half of her home. The four-storey, six-bedroom home in east London has been valued at £2.1m. His siblings say their mother could not have understood what she was signing because she was "desperately unwell". In January 2023 she was given a terminal diagnosis of stage four metastatic colorectal cancer. The claimants also allege that Mrs Nessa, who was nearly blind and could not speak English, was unaware of what she was signing because the documents were not translated into her native Bengali at the time they were signed. Kashim Chowdhury denies the claims. That case is ongoing. Additional reporting by Ben Sturt.

items.articleText: İran'dan savaş resti: "ABD ve İsrail'i bekleyen sürprizler var" - İran Genelkurmay Başkanı Tümgeneral Ali Abdullahi, ABD ve İsrail'le olası yeni bir çatışmada "birçok sürprizin ardı ardına ortaya çıkacağını" söyledi. - Abdullahi, İran'ın hedef alınması halinde karşılık vereceklerini belirtti. İran ile ABD ve İsrail arasındaki gerilim sürerken Tahran'dan yeni bir açıklama geldi. İran Genelkurmay Başkanı Tümgeneral Ali Abdullahi, olası bir savaşın yeniden başlaması halinde karşı tarafı bekleyen sürprizler olacağını ifade etti. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle İran resmi haber ajansı IRNA'nın aktardığına göre Abdullahi, Devrim Muhafızları Ordusunun yeni yer altı füze üssünün tanıtım töreninde konuştu. ABD ve İsrail'in tehditlerine değinen Abdullahi, düşmanın askeri gücünün ve sahip olduğu tesislerin İran'ın kararlarını etkilemeyeceğini söyledi. "Gelecekteki savaşta sürprizler olacak" İsrail Başbakanı Binyamin Netanyahu'nun İran'a yönelik açıklamalarına da yanıt veren Abdullahi, Netanyahu'nun "Ya İran'ı yok edeceğiz ya da İran bizi yok edecek" sözlerini hatırlattı. Abdullahi, İran'ın bu tehditlere boyun eğmeyeceğini belirterek, "Onları kesinlikle yok edeceğimiz açıktır" ifadelerini kullandı. İranlı komutan, önceki çatışmalarda ABD ve İsrail'in sahip oldukları askeri imkanları kullandıklarını ancak hedeflerine ulaşamadıklarını öne sürdü. Abdullahi, konuşmasını olası yeni çatışmaya ilişkin şu sözlerle tamamladı: "Gelecekteki savaşta sürprizler ardı ardına ortaya çıkacak."

items.titleTr: Here’s what happened in crypto today
items.summaryTr: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
items.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, Coinbase and Kalshi have joined four other firms backing the CFTC in a lawsuit over whether US exchanges can list perpetual futures tied to individual stocks, cybersecurity firm CertiK urged exchanges to impose hard dollar limits on hot-wallet holdings following the $6.3 billion Binance hack, and blockchain analytics firm Elliptic reported that North Korean hackers used newly created memecoins to launder stolen funds. Coinbase, Kalshi join lawsuit backing CFTC over US stock perp futures Coinbase, Kalshi and four other companies asked a federal court Monday to accept a brief backing the United States Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) in a lawsuit over perpetual futures tied to individual US stocks. According to a proposed amicus brief shared Monday by Coinbase legal representative Molly Abraham, the group also includes Kraken parent Payward, trading companies DRW Holdings and Jump Trading, and crypto investment company Paradigm Operations. The companies argue that stock perpetual futures fall under existing US futures laws. The filing comes days after a federal judge found that the CFTC likely “exceeded its statutory authority” in allowing single-stock perpetuals to trade as security futures. The case could determine whether US exchanges can offer retail traders contracts that track individual stocks without expiring. On Nov. 3, the CFTC announced that single-stock perpetual futures, or stock perps, could begin trading on US-regulated exchanges for the first time. The Capital Markets Alliance Association (CMAA), a newly formed trade and advocacy group representing traditional financial market participants and whose members include Cboe and Citadel Securities, sued the CFTC last week, challenging the CFTC’s authority to allow the contracts to trade. Crypto exchanges need dollar caps on hot wallets, CertiK says Crypto exchanges should impose hard dollar limits on their hot-wallet holdings rather than relying solely on cold-storage ratios to measure security, according to cybersecurity firm CertiK. The recommendation came as several crypto exchanges recently disclosed how much they held in cold wallets, seeking to reassure customers after the record Binance hack that targeted its hot wallets. Crypto exchange Gate reported that 88.26% of its total assets were in cold storage, while Coinbase said it keeps more than 99% of customer assets offline. “Cold storage is a useful measure of online exposure, but it is not a standalone security score,” CertiK’s research team told Cointelegraph. CertiK said crypto exchanges should consider setting hot-wallet caps for each asset and blockchain according to the strictest of three limits: a percentage of customer liabilities, estimated withdrawal needs and an absolute loss ceiling based on the exchange’s financial resources and recovery capabilities. “Flexibility should support operating liquidity, while hard dollar ceilings and circuit breakers limit potential loss,” they said. North Korean hackers create memecoins to launder funds from Binance hack: Elliptic North Korean hackers created memecoins to launder cryptocurrency stolen in the $6.3 billion Binance hack, routing roughly $430,000 through six newly launched tokens on the NEAR blockchain, according to a report from blockchain analytics firm Elliptic. Between Nov. 5 and 7, the hackers created at least six tokens on NEAR and used liquidity pools on decentralized exchanges to move stolen funds between wallets, Elliptic said. The tokens attracted almost no outside trading and were abandoned shortly after launch. The hackers used one set of wallets to swap stolen NEAR tokens for the new memecoins, then used another set to sell those memecoins back into the pools for NEAR. The swaps let them move funds without direct wallet-to-wallet transfers, though the transactions remained traceable onchain. Elliptic said the same laundering technique was also used following the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in 2025, when North Korean-linked actors moved at least $24 million through a newly created token on the TRON blockchain.

items.title: Bitcoin’s ‘best buying opportunity ever’ has arrived: Mark Moss
items.summary: Bitcoin Opportunity Fund co-founder Mark Moss says that with banks and ETFs widening access to Bitcoin he expects a new record high in 2027.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Bitcoin’s ‘best buying opportunity ever’ has arrived: Mark Moss
items.summaryTr: Bitcoin Opportunity Fund co-founder Mark Moss says that with banks and ETFs widening access to Bitcoin he expects a new record high in 2027.
items.articleText: Bitcoin’s ‘best buying opportunity ever’ has arrived: Mark Moss Bitcoin Opportunity Fund co-founder Mark Moss says that with banks and ETFs widening access to Bitcoin he expects a new record high in 2027. Wall Street’s embrace of Bitcoin has created the “best buying opportunity ever,” according to investor Mark Moss. Moss co-founded the Bitcoin Opportunity Fund, where he is an advisory partner. In 2025, UK-listed Satsuma Technology appointed him chief Bitcoin strategist. Moss tells Cointelegraph on the latest episode of Trade Secrets that he first bought Bitcoin in 2015 at about $300, during a recovery from a $1,000 to $200 plunge. “It was so risky,” Moss recalls of buying back then. In contrast, today, “you have consensus from the US government and Wall Street.” “But most people still think it’s a scam,” he says. That skepticism opens buying opportunities as Bitcoin starts to cross what Moss calls the “chasm” between early adopters and mainstream investors. Banks and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have made Bitcoin easier to buy and financial advisers could help persuade clients who have stayed away previously to consider investing. Related: Strategy shareholders approve daily dividends for four preferred stocks Moss calls bottom but Bitcoin keeps falling Bitcoin briefly climbed above $80,000 after the Democrats took control of the US Congress in the midterm elections, then gave back those gains as tech stocks sold off. By Friday, it fell to $74,762, its lowest level since August and remains in the doldrums at the time of writing. Despite the selloff, Moss points to the reaction to the $6.3 billion Binance hack as a sign that sellers were running out. “The price didn’t really drop,” he says. Bitcoin fell to $76,320 after the breach and slid to $74,762 on Friday, erasing its post-election gains. It fell further to about $73,500 late Sunday, its lowest level since August, after Nvidia’s board announced it would investigate reports that CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. Bitcoin found another bottom after reports of Nvidia CEO’s scandal. Source: CoinMarketCap Flows into US spot Bitcoin ETFs swung sharply during election week. The funds took in about $75 million on Wednesday, then shed $430 million on Thursday. History is on the side of hodlers however. Bitcoin gained an average of about 53% in the 12 months after previous US midterms, Moss says, using data going back to 2014. That leaves three completed election cycles in his sample. He says he expects Bitcoin to set a new all-time high in 2027. Moss backs Strategy but would keep his Bitcoin Moss thinks the Bitcoin treasury company to own is Strategy (MSTR), but believes that holding Bitcoin yourself is still superior. Strategy began buying Bitcoin in 2020 and turned those purchases into a core part of its business. It has used stock and debt sales to fund its purchases, giving investors a way to bet on Bitcoin through a publicly traded company. By Nov. 2, Strategy held 849,327 BTC, more than 4% of Bitcoin’s maximum supply. “I don’t think there’s another publicly traded company that will outperform Strategy over the next ten years,” Moss says. Strategy has the world’s largest corporate Bitcoin trove. Source: BitcoinTreasuries.Net Leverage can help a Bitcoin treasury company’s shares outperform the cryptocurrency it holds when its price rises. But even if Strategy outperforms, Moss wouldn’t trade his Bitcoin holdings for its shares. Related: 1inch lawyer sees agencies driving US crypto regulation as midterms unfold Before Moss bought his first Bitcoin, he made a living buying foreclosed properties, fixing them up and selling them. He moved into property development, then built and sold a medical equipment business. He says he put the proceeds into Southern California real estate. When the market crashed in 2008, he lost it all. “The reward of being right is not worth the risk of getting it wrong,” he says. Even with his outlook for Strategy, Moss says he’d keep his Bitcoin and use only a small share of his portfolio to pursue higher returns through treasury stocks. A journey of $1 million Bitcoin starts with small allocations In Moss’s model, Bitcoin could reach $1 million under certain circumstances, when it competes with stocks, bonds, gold and real estate for a considerable share of investors’ wealth. The model estimates how much those assets are worth, projects how that pool could grow as the global money supply expands and calculates a Bitcoin price based on the share it captures. Financial advisers could help bring in that money via one client’s portfolio at a time, encouraging them to shift a few percentage points out of stocks or bonds and into Bitcoin. The scenario depends on a critical mass of clients doing that, to the point where all those small allocations add up. The model also assumes Bitcoin stays secure and decentralized. Asked what could derail the scenario, Moss pointed to a failure that compromised either feature. Moss says $1 million is possible by 2030... though hodler’s might have to wait until 2032. Hodler’s Digest: Vitalik ‘pivots’ ETH to store of value, crypto suffers after US midterms

items.summaryTr: With 30 men under her orders, she organised sabotage operations, sheltered Allied airmen and joined the fight against the occupying German forces.
items.articleText: French wartime resistance heroine Solange Alexandre dies aged 104 - Published One of France's last Resistance heroes from World War Two has died at the age of 104. Solange Alexandre was also a rare woman who, with her future husband, created and commanded her own unit of anti-German fighters. After serving as a Resistance courier from 1941, three years later she founded the Pas-de-Boeuf network near the town of Ruillé-sur-Loir. With some 30 men under her orders, she organised sabotage operations, sheltered Allied airmen and, after the Allied landings in Normandy on D-Day in 1944, joined the fight against the occupying German forces. President Emmanuel Macron was among many to pay tribute to Alexandre, after her death was announced at a nursing home in Le Mans. "She said she only ever did her duty. But her duty was our freedom. France will never forget. Thank you," Macron posted on social media. Born in 1922 in the Sarthe department of western France, Solange Alexandre, née Dubuisson, grew up in a patriotic family that had suffered in World War One. "My mother lost her first husband in the war, and my father was wounded in 1917. The words homeland and honour were very important to us. They were in my blood," she recalled in her memoirs. In June 1940 she heard on the radio the appeal from General Charles de Gaulle in London, calling on the French not to give up the struggle against Germany. She had never heard of him, but that did not matter. "From that moment I knew I had to join up," she wrote. Some months later she was recruited by a friend of her father's – a Tunisian-born French army veteran called Saïd Belhaffaf, who had joined the Resistance. Using the code-name Corlay, she criss-crossed the region around Le Mans by bicycle, gathering information and passing on messages. "There were no mobile phones back then, and no private cars either because of the lack of petrol. The bicycle was king," she said in an interview two years ago. In 1943 she met her first husband Guy Déliot, who had deserted from the French gendarmerie after refusing to arrest some Jews. The following April, with the Allied invasion approaching, they decided to take to the maquis, in other words live clandestinely in the forested hills, supplied with food by local farmers. Their group consisted of deserters from German forced labour programmes, as well as survivors from another Resistance outfit that had been destroyed by the enemy. There were also two airmen, one American and one Canadian. "Twice the Gestapo came for me, and twice I slipped through their hands," she later recalled. Solange Alexandre was also a rare woman who, with her future husband, created and commanded her own unit of anti-German fighters. After serving as a Resistance courier from 1941, three years later she founded the Pas-de-Boeuf network near the town of Ruillé-sur-Loir. With some 30 men under her orders, she organised sabotage operations, sheltered Allied airmen and, after the Allied landings in Normandy on D-Day in 1944, joined the fight against the occupying German forces. President Emmanuel Macron was among many to pay tribute to Alexandre, after her death was announced at a nursing home in Le Mans. "She said she only ever did her duty. But her duty was our freedom. France will never forget. Thank you," Macron posted on social media. Born in 1922 in the Sarthe department of western France, Solange Alexandre, née Dubuisson, grew up in a patriotic family that had suffered in World War One. "My mother lost her first husband in the war, and my father was wounded in 1917. The words homeland and honour were very important to us. They were in my blood," she recalled in her memoirs. She had never heard of him, but that did not matter. "From that moment I knew I had to join up," she wrote. items.summaryTr: A local hospital says runners had "unusual" symptoms after racing on an atypically hot day.
items.articleText: California police investigate after 27 fall ill at half-marathon running event - Published Police in Santa Barbara, California, are investigating after nearly 30 people had to seek medical care at a half-marathon running event held in the city on Sunday. In a statement provided to the BBC's US partner CBS News, officers said they received a report from Santa Barbara Cottage Hospital about race participants who sought medical treatment "for unusual symptoms" after the race ended. "The cause of the reported symptoms has not been confirmed," the statement added. Cottage Health, which operates the hospital, told CBS it had seen "a larger than expected number of emergency visits" from those who ran the race. "There is no specific action recommended for the public at this time; however, participants who feel unwell should seek medical attention and follow guidance from healthcare professionals," police said. Cottage Hospital said it treated 27 people from the half marathon at emergency rooms in Santa Barbara and the nearby city of Goleta. The vast majority of them - 24 - were discharged after treatment, while three people were still in hospital as of Monday in stable condition. Several thousand people ran the half marathon on a hotter-than-usual day in Santa Barbara along the Pacific Ocean. Temperatures reportedly reached 86F (27C) by midday, compared to a typical early November temperature of low 70s. One of the runners who went to hospital told local news outlet KEYT-TV that they had lost consciousness and could not remember parts of the race. "It is awfully suspicious," said the runner, who declined to be identified. "We had people saying they were hallucinating." "I am not too familiar with heat exhaustion but I have never seen anyone not remembering a long portion of their run," the runner added. Event director David Monico told US media that 15 people were taken from the medical tent to local hospitals because of dehydration and overheating. The BBC has contacted the Santa Barbara Police Department, Cottage Health and the half marathon organisers for further comment. Related topics - Published6 days ago - Published6 days ago

items.summaryTr: Avrupalı Türk Markalar Birliği Başkanı Vehbi Keleş, kendi şirketinin de siber saldırıya uğradığını açıklayarak işletmeleri uyardı. İngiltere'de 158 yıllık, 700 çalışanlı bir şirketin siber saldırı sonrası iflas ettiğini belirten Keleş, alınması gereken önlemleri anlattı.
items.articleText: Türk iş insanından siber saldırı uyarısı: İngiltere'de 158 yıllık şirket iflas etti - Avrupalı Türk Markalar Birliği Başkanı Vehbi Keleş, kendi şirketinin de siber saldırıya uğradığını açıklayarak işletmeleri uyardı. İngiltere'de 158 yıllık, 700 çalışanlı bir şirketin siber saldırı sonrası iflas ettiğini belirten Keleş, alınması gereken önlemleri anlattı. Avrupalı Türk Markalar Birliği (ATMB) Başkanı Vehbi Keleş, CNBC-e Londra Temsilcisi Berfu Güven'in canlı yayında yönelttiği soruları yanıtladı. İngiltere'deki Türk markalarının 2026 yılındaki performansını değerlendiren Keleş, artan enerji ve nakliye maliyetleri, tüketicilerin stok yapma eğilimi, siber saldırılar ve Türkiye ile İngiltere arasındaki ticari ilişkiler hakkında açıklamalarda bulundu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Enerji maliyetlerindeki artışın önce nakliyeye, ardından üretime ve diğer alanlara yansıdığını belirten Keleş, Türk markalarını en fazla zorlayan unsurun nakliye maliyetleri olduğunu söyledi. Nakliye giderlerinin petrol fiyatlarına bağlı olduğunu ifade eden Keleş, Kızıldeniz'de yaşanan sorunlar nedeniyle sevkiyat sürelerinin de uzayabildiğini kaydetti. Türkiye dahil 36 ülkeden ürün getirerek İngiltere pazarında satışa sunduklarını belirten Keleş, tüketicilerin evde stok yapmaya yönelik çağrılarının satışlara etkisini de değerlendirdi. Makarna, bakliyat ve konserve satışlarında yüzde 40'a varan artış İngiltere'de stok yapma çağrılarının ardından bazı ürün gruplarında satışların arttığını belirten Keleş, ancak pandemi dönemindekine benzer bir kaos yaşanmadığını söyledi. Makarna, bakliyat ve konserve gibi ürünlerin satışlarında yüzde 20 ile yüzde 40 arasında artış görüldüğünü ifade eden Keleş, bunun tüketimin aynı oranda arttığı anlamına gelmediğini vurguladı. Satın alınan ürünlerin evlerde bekletildiğini belirten Keleş, öne çekilen alışverişlerin ilerleyen dönemlerde satışların yavaşlamasına neden olabileceğini söyledi. Pandemi döneminin şirketler açısından önemli bir tecrübe olduğunu ifade eden Keleş, Türk markalarının mevcut sürece hazırlıklı olduğunu dile getirdi. "Siber saldırıyı ben yaşadım" Avrupa'da yaşanan siber saldırıların şu aşamada Türk markaları açısından bir sorun oluşturmadığını belirten Keleş, kendi şirketinin de geçen yıl siber saldırıya uğradığını açıkladı. Saldırının ardından şirketin sistemlerine erişilemediğini anlatan Keleş, müşteri listeleri ve adresler dahil birçok veriye ulaşılamadığını söyledi. Yedekleme sisteminin de saldırıdan etkilendiğini belirten Keleş, çalışanlarına her akşam USB belleklere manuel yedek almalarını söylediğini ifade etti. Bu yedekler sayesinde ertesi gün sistemleri yeniden kurabildiklerini aktaran Keleş, şirketin veri kaybı yaşamadan faaliyetlerine devam ettiğini belirtti. Saldırı sonrasında yeni sunucular ve güvenlik duvarları için 30-40 bin civarında bir maliyet oluştuğunu söyleyen Keleş, asıl büyük riskin şirketin tamamen kaybedilmesi olduğunu vurguladı. İngiltere'de yaklaşık 158 yıllık geçmişe ve 700 çalışana sahip bir nakliye şirketinin siber saldırı sonrasında iflas ettiğini belirten Keleş, manuel yedekleme sistemleri bulunmasaydı kendi şirketlerinin de çok büyük maliyetlerle karşılaşabileceğini söyledi. "Bana olmaz demeyin" uyarısı İnternete bağlı her sistemin siber saldırılara açık olduğunu belirten Keleş, şirketleri güvenlik önlemleri konusunda uyardı. Özellikle soğuk hava depolarında kullanılan cihazların fabrika çıkış şifrelerinin değiştirilmesi gerektiğini söyleyen Keleş, bu cihazlar için yeni ve güvenli şifreler oluşturulmasının önemine dikkat çekti. Fransa'da yaşanan bir siber saldırının ardından İngiltere'deki üç soğuk hava deposunun da saldırıya uğradığını belirten Keleş, kendi şirketlerine yönelik saldırının Ukrayna üzerinden geldiğini ancak bunun saldırıyı gerçekleştiren kişinin Ukraynalı olduğu anlamına gelmediğini ifade etti. Stok çağrıları raf fiyatlarına yansımadı Stok yapma çağrılarının ve şirketlerin aldığı ek tedbirlerin şu aşamada raf fiyatlarına yansımadığını belirten Keleş, tüketicilerin paniğe kapılmasına gerek olmadığını söyledi. Keleş, sürecin normal seyrinde devam etmesi halinde ilave maliyetlerin de raf fiyatlarına yansımayabileceğini ifade etti. Türkiye ile İngiltere arasındaki yeni anlaşma için 2027 beklentisi Türkiye ile İngiltere arasında müzakere edilen yeni serbest ticaret anlaşmasına ilişkin de değerlendirmelerde bulunan Keleş, imza takviminin henüz netleşmediğini söyledi. Anlaşmanın büyük ihtimalle 2027 yılının ilk altı ayında imzalanmasını beklediklerini belirten Keleş, iki ülke arasındaki dış ticaret verilerini de paylaştı. Ekim sonu itibarıyla Türkiye'nin İngiltere'ye ihracatında yüzde 2,2 düşüş görüldüğünü ifade eden Keleş, Birleşik Krallık'ın Türkiye'ye ihracatında ise yüzde 2,9 artış yaşandığını belirtti. Sektörel verilere de değinen Keleş, Türkiye'nin İngiltere'ye ihracatında gıdada yüzde 3, hazır giyimde yüzde 7 ve mobilyada yüzde 2 düşüş görüldüğünü söyledi. Otomotiv sektöründe de gerileme yaşandığını ifade etti. Buna karşılık elektrik ve elektronik sektöründe yüzde 11, çelik sektöründe ise yaklaşık yüzde 60 artış kaydedildiğini belirtti. Türk markaları İngiliz marketlerinde neden etnik ürün raflarında kalıyor? Yaklaşık 20 yıldır İngiltere'deki zincir marketlere ürün verdiklerini belirten Keleş, Türk markalarının bu pazarda karşılaştığı sorunlara da değindi. Türkiye'nin küresel ölçekte tanınan bir markasının bulunmamasının zincir marketlerdeki konumlarını etkilediğini söyleyen Keleş, Türk ürünlerinin çoğunlukla etnik ürün raflarında yer aldığını ifade etti. Türkiye'de çok büyük olan bir markanın İngiliz market zincirleri açısından daha önce hiç karşılaşılmamış bir ürün olabileceğini belirten Keleş, markaların uluslararası pazarlarda tanınması için küreselleşmeye ve marka yatırımlarına önem verilmesi gerektiğini söyledi. 2027'de fiyatlar düşebilir İngiltere'deki Türk markalarının 2027 yılına ilişkin beklentilerini de paylaşan Keleş, mevcut sorunların çözülmesi halinde fiyatların yeniden düşmeye başlayabileceğini ifade etti. Keleş, 2027 yılının herkesin güzel ticaret yaptığı önemli bir yıl olmasını umut ettiklerini söyledi.

Türkiye'de çok büyük olan bir markanın İngiliz market zincirleri açısından daha önce hiç karşılaşılmamış bir ürün olabileceğini belirten Keleş, markaların uluslararası pazarlarda tanınması için küreselleşmeye ve marka yatırımlarına önem verilmesi gerektiğini söyledi. 2027'de fiyatlar düşebilir İngiltere'deki Türk markalarının 2027 yılına ilişkin beklentilerini de paylaşan Keleş, mevcut sorunların çözülmesi halinde fiyatların yeniden düşmeye başlayabileceğini ifade etti. Keleş, 2027 yılının herkesin güzel ticaret yaptığı önemli bir yıl olmasını umut ettiklerini söyledi.

items.summaryTr: ABD'de Tüketici Fiyat Endeksi (TÜFE), ekimde aylık yüzde 0,4 arttı. Böylece aylık enflasyon eylüldeki yüzde 0,6 seviyesinden gerilerken, gıda ve enerji hariç çekirdek TÜFE yüzde 0,3 yükseldi.
items.articleText: Piyasaların odağındaki veri açıklandı: ABD'de enflasyon beklentileri aştı ABD'de Tüketici Fiyat Endeksi (TÜFE), ekimde aylık yüzde 0,4 arttı. Böylece aylık enflasyon eylüldeki yüzde 0,6 seviyesinden gerilerken, gıda ve enerji hariç çekirdek TÜFE yüzde 0,3 yükseldi. ABD Çalışma İstatistikleri Bürosu, ağustos ayına ilişkin tüketici fiyat endeksi verilerini açıkladı. ABD'de enflasyon beklentileri aştı ABD'de tüketicilerin kısa, orta ve uzun vadeli enflasyon beklentileri Ekim ayında değişmeyerek sırasıyla yüzde 3,9, yüzde 3,3 ve yüzde 3 seviyelerinde kalmıştı. Açıklanan verilere göre ABD'de Tüketici Fiyat Endeksi (TÜFE), ekim ayında aylık bazda yüzde 0,4 artarak eylüldeki yüzde 0,6'lık yükselişin altında gerçekleşti. ABD Çalışma İstatistikleri Bürosu (BLS), Ekim 2026 dönemine ilişkin tüketici fiyat endeksi verilerini açıkladı. Buna göre, Tüketici Fiyat Endeksi ekimde mevsim etkilerinden arındırılmış olarak aylık bazda yüzde 0,4 arttı. Endeks, eylül ayında yüzde 0,6 yükselmişti. Barınma endeksi ekimde yüzde 0,3 artarken, bu kalem aylık enflasyondaki toplam yükselişin yüzde 30'undan fazlasını oluşturdu. Gıda endeksi aynı dönemde yüzde 0,5 artış kaydetti. Evde tüketilen gıda fiyatları yüzde 0,4, dışarıda tüketilen gıda fiyatları ise yüzde 0,5 yükseldi. Enerji endeksi de ekimde yüzde 0,7 arttı. Söz konusu endekste eylül ayında yüzde 5,2'lik artış yaşanmıştı. Çekirdek enflasyon yüzde 0,3 arttı Gıda ve enerji kalemlerinin hariç tutulduğu çekirdek TÜFE, ekimde aylık bazda yüzde 0,3 yükseldi. Çekirdek enflasyondaki artış ağustos ve eylül aylarında da yüzde 0,3 olarak kaydedilmişti. Ekim ayında eğlence, sağlık hizmetleri, motorlu taşıt sigortası, ev eşyaları ve hizmetleri ile eğitim kalemlerinde fiyat artışları görüldü. Buna karşılık, kullanılmış otomobil ve kamyon fiyatları ile iletişim endeksinde düşüş kaydedildi.

items.title: Bitcoin may benefit as global tightening slows, Binance Research says
items.summary: Binance Research says Bitcoin could find support as global monetary tightening slows, even as markets price in a December Fed rate hike.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Bitcoin may benefit as global tightening slows, Binance Research says
items.summaryTr: Binance Research says Bitcoin could find support as global monetary tightening slows, even as markets price in a December Fed rate hike.
items.articleText: Bitcoin may benefit as global tightening slows, Binance Research says Binance Research says Bitcoin could find support as global monetary tightening slows, even as markets price in a December Fed rate hike. Bitcoin could find support before major central banks start cutting rates if the spread of rate hikes continues to slow, Binance Research said Tuesday. Eight of the 10 central banks Binance tracks had raised rates over the last six months, including Sweden’s announced increase on Nov. 4, with the momentum of tightening starting to ease since its July peak, Binance Research said in a Tuesday report shared with Cointelegraph. “Whether this easing continues into early 2027 will be key to judging whether the macro backdrop is turning less hostile for crypto,” the report said. Binance pointed to the previous cycle. Bitcoin (BTC) bottomed in November 2022, and its six-month return turned positive in February 2023, before any of the central banks in the index began cutting rates. Pace of G10 banks tightening and Bitcoin’s 6-month returns. Source: Binance Research Similarly, in 2024, monetary tightening measures led to Bitcoin delivering its “strongest” six-month return of the cycle, exceeding 160% in March, Binance said. “In each case, BTC moved with the direction of global policy, not its level,” the report adds. Related: Analysts see no broader ‘contagion’ from $6.3B Binance hack December rate hike odds mount following Waller’s speech A US rate increase remains in play. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said Tuesday he was leaning toward a quarter-point hike in December and would consider a half-point move if core inflation remained elevated. Odds of a 25-basis-point hike in December rose from 76.3% to 96.3% on Tuesday, according to CME Group’s FedWatch Tool. In a Nov. 2 report, Bitwise also argued that a slowdown in economic growth expectations could eventually prompt central banks to pivot towards easing monetary policy, potentially creating a more favourable environment for Bitcoin. BTC/USD, 1-year chart. Source: CoinMarketCap Bitcoin’s price fell 3.5% during the past week, extending its one-year decline to 30%. The world’s first cryptocurrency was trading at $74,131, or 41% below its $126,198 all-time high, according to CoinMarketCap. Magazine: Wall Street killed Bitcoin’s wild rallies: 10x’s Markus Thielen

items.summary: Goldman Sachs CEO'su David Solomon, yapay zeka altyapısına yönelik yatırımların geri dönüşüne ilişkin soru işaretlerine rağmen finansman talebinin güçlü seyrettiğini söyledi. Solomon, yapay zekanın uzun vadede ekonomide verimliliği artıracağına inandığını vurguladı.

items.summaryTr: Goldman Sachs CEO'su David Solomon, yapay zeka altyapısına yönelik yatırımların geri dönüşüne ilişkin soru işaretlerine rağmen finansman talebinin güçlü seyrettiğini söyledi. Solomon, yapay zekanın uzun vadede ekonomide verimliliği artıracağına inandığını vurguladı.
items.articleText: Goldman Sachs CEO'su açıkladı: Yapay zekaya milyarlarca dolarlık talep sürüyor - Goldman Sachs CEO'su David Solomon, yapay zeka altyapısına yönelik yatırımların geri dönüşüne ilişkin soru işaretlerine rağmen finansman talebinin güçlü seyrettiğini söyledi. Goldman Sachs Üst Yöneticisi (CEO) David Solomon, yapay zeka sektöründeki yatırım iştahının sürdüğünü belirtti. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle CNBC'ye konuşan Solomon, yatırımcıların altyapı harcamalarının geri dönüşünü yeniden değerlendirdiği bir dönemde, yapay zeka sermaye piyasası işlemlerinde son haftalarda oldukça aktif olduklarını söyledi. Solomon, yapay zeka altyapısının kurulmasına ve teknolojinin büyümesini destekleyen yatırımlara yönelik talebin güçlü kalmaya devam ettiğini ifade etti. Yapay zeka hisselerinde satış baskısı Solomon, siyasi ortamda yaşanan değişimlerin piyasada yeniden ayarlamalara ve dalgalanmalara yol açabileceğini belirtti. Buna karşın yapay zekanın ekonomide verimliliği artırma potansiyeline ilişkin uzun vadeli iyimserliğini koruduğunu dile getirdi. Çip üreticileri ve yeni nesil bulut hizmeti sağlayıcıları dahil olmak üzere yapay zeka bağlantılı hisseler, son haftalarda sert satışlarla karşılaştı. Yatırımcılar, sektöre aktarılan yüz milyarlarca dolarlık sermayenin yeterli getiri sağlayıp sağlamayacağını sorgulamaya başladı. ABD ara seçimleri öncesinde başlayan satış baskısı, Demokratların seçimlerde elde ettiği sonuçların ardından sektör üzerindeki siyasi baskının artabileceği endişesiyle derinleşti. Anthropic'in halka arz süreci yakından izleniyor Piyasa algısındaki değişim, halka arza hazırlanan yapay zeka şirketi Anthropic açısından da önemli bir döneme denk geldi. Goldman Sachs, şirketin halka arz sürecine liderlik eden bankalar arasında bulunuyor. Yapay zeka yatırımlarında veri merkezleri, çipler, enerji altyapısı ve bulut hizmetleri için yapılan harcamalar öne çıkıyor. Yatırımcıların odağında ise bu yüksek maliyetli yatırımların ne zaman ve hangi ölçüde gelir ve kâra dönüşeceği bulunuyor.

items.articleText: Fon soruşturmasında yeni gelişme: 5 şüpheli adliyeye sevk edildi - Sermaye piyasalarındaki işlemlere ilişkin fon soruşturması kapsamında gözaltına alınan OMG Capital Advisors, Takasbank, Bulls Yatırım, Ruzy Madencilik ve Lydia Holding yöneticilerinin de aralarında bulunduğu 5 şüpheli adliyeye sevk edildi. Sermaye piyasalarında gerçekleştirilen işlemlere ilişkin yürütülen fon soruşturması kapsamında yeni bir gelişme yaşandı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Soruşturmada gözaltına alınan 5 şüpheli adliyeye sevk edildi. İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığınca sermaye piyasalarında gerçekleştirilen işlemlere ilişkin fon soruşturması devam ediyor. Soruşturma kapsamında gözaltına alınan OMG Capital Advisors Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Ömer Murat Gülkan, eski Takasbank Genel Müdürü Yunus Arıncı, Bulls Yatırım Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Kemal Akkaya, Ruzy Madencilik Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Nureddin Çevik ve Lydia Holding Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Enver Çevik'in emniyetteki işlemleri tamamlandı. Sağlık kontrolünün ardından Çağlayan'daki İstanbul Adliyesi'ne getirilen şüphelilerin savcılıktaki işlemleri sürüyor.

items.articleText: Rusya'dan teknoloji devlerine ceza: Apple, Google ve Telegram'a milyonluk yaptırım - Rusya'da mahkeme, yasaklı içerikleri kaldırmadıkları gerekçesiyle Apple, Google, Telegram ve Wikimedia Vakfına toplam 26,3 milyon ruble (yaklaşık 318 bin dolar) para cezası verdi. items.title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government
items.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu's main political rival, Gadi Eisenkot, has first chance to build a new government and oust the prime minister.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government
items.summaryTr: Benjamin Netanyahu's main political rival, Gadi Eisenkot, has first chance to build a new government and oust the prime minister.
items.articleText: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government - Published Israel's new parliament will be sworn in on Tuesday, as opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot seeks to oust caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The former army chief was tasked with forming a government by the president, after he received the backing of 67 members of the 120-seat Knesset, compared to 46 for Netanyahu. But Eisenkot faces an uphill struggle. His bloc of four parties won 48 seats in last month's election, while Netanyahu's bloc won 53, leaving both short of a majority. He has 28 days to build a coalition, with a possible two-week extension. Almost half of the MKs being sworn in did not serve in the previous parliament, while Arab-led parties have a record number of seats. The outcome of the election, which was widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu, means there is a period of uncertainty over who will form the next government. Netanyahu will remain caretaker prime minister until then - a process which could take from days to months. One of the most dramatic results was the performance of Israel's two Arab-led alliances - the United Arab List and the Joint List - which won an unprecedented 19 seats between them following a surge in turnout among Arab voters. The Arab parties could therefore hold the balance of power, although Netanyahu has ruled out governing with them and three of the parties in Eisenkot's bloc have opposed including them in a coalition. On Sunday, President Isaac Herzog tasked Eisenkot with trying to form a government. Speaking at the president's residence, the centrist Yashar party leader called for the formation of a "national emergency government" - an implicit appeal to parties to put ideological differences aside to remove Netanyahu from office. This, he said, would "require creative and unconventional political steps". Eisenkot said any party or MK prepared to accept four principles could join his proposed government. Those are recognition of Israel as a Jewish and democratic state; accepting the values of the Declaration of Independence; backing mandatory military, national or civilian service for all, including communities currently exempt; and recognising Hamas as a terrorist organisation and committing to dismantling its military and governing capabilities. The four requirements, however, could present significant obstacles to Eisenkot's potential partners. The conscription of ultra-Orthodox Jewish men, who are exempt from military service if they are in full-time religious study, was a major election issue. The ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism (UTJ) and Shas parties, which won 13 seats in total, have fiercely objected to attempts to change the status quo - something that all parties in Eisenkot's bloc campaigned to do. Eisenkot's four principles are also contentious for the Arab parties. Both emphasise equal national and civic rights for Israel's Arab citizens, who form about 20% of the population; the vast majority of Israeli Arabs are not required to serve in the military; and neither has publicly recognised Hamas as a terrorist organisation. The Arab parties could, though, help Eisenkot form a minority government. The United Arab List, which won eight seats, has said it is willing to be part of an Eisenkot-led coalition, while the Joint List, which won 11 seats, has offered parliamentary support from the outside. If Eisenkot accepted such an arrangement, he would still have to persuade other parties in his bloc to agree. Avigdor Lieberman, whose Yisrael Beiteinu party won seven seats, has so far refused to join a minority government dependent on Arab MKs. In return for their support, the ultra-Orthodox parties would be likely to demand major concessions on military conscription, which might be unacceptable to most of the parties in Eisenkot's bloc. Netanyahu - Israel's longest-serving leader - reiterated in a video on Monday his call for the formation of a government of national unity, which he said he would lead as prime minister. He said any Zionist party - those which support Israel as a Jewish state - including opposition parties, would be eligible. He warned against a government which relied on what he called "the Islamists", an apparent reference to Arab parties. "You cannot form a government with Hamas supporters," he said. items.title: Coinbase, Kalshi join lawsuit backing CFTC over US stock perp futures
items.summary: Coinbase, Kalshi and four other companies backed the CFTC in a lawsuit over whether US exchanges can list perpetual futures tied to individual stocks.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Coinbase, Kalshi join lawsuit backing CFTC over US stock perp futures
items.summaryTr: Coinbase, Kalshi and four other companies backed the CFTC in a lawsuit over whether US exchanges can list perpetual futures tied to individual stocks.
items.articleText: Coinbase, Kalshi join lawsuit backing CFTC over US stock perp futures Coinbase, Kalshi and four other companies backed the CFTC in a lawsuit over whether US exchanges can list perpetual futures tied to individual stocks. Coinbase, Kalshi and four other companies asked a federal court Monday to accept a brief backing the United States Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) in a lawsuit over perpetual futures tied to individual US stocks. According to a proposed amicus brief shared Monday by Coinbase legal representative Molly Abraham, the group also includes Kraken parent Payward, trading companies DRW Holdings and Jump Trading, and crypto investment company Paradigm Operations. The companies argue that stock perpetual futures fall under existing US futures laws. The filing comes days after a federal judge found that the CFTC likely “exceeded its statutory authority” in allowing single-stock perpetuals to trade as security futures. The case could determine whether US exchanges can offer retail traders contracts that track individual stocks without expiring. Why stock perps face scrutiny On Nov. 3, the CFTC announced that single-stock perpetual futures, or stock perps, could begin trading on US-regulated exchanges for the first time. The Capital Markets Alliance Association (CMAA), a newly formed trade and advocacy group representing traditional financial market participants and whose members include Cboe and Citadel Securities, sued the CFTC last week, challenging the CFTC’s authority to allow the contracts to trade. Stock perps allow traders to speculate on the price movements of individual stocks without owning the shares. Unlike traditional futures, they have no fixed expiration date. The CMAA argues that because the contracts lack a fixed expiration date, they should be regulated as security-based swaps, a type of derivative linked to stocks or other securities that is primarily overseen by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and faces tighter restrictions on retail trading. The six companies backing the CFTC disagree, arguing that a fixed expiration date is not required for a contract to qualify as a security future, which falls under joint CFTC and SEC oversight. Related: Coinbase’s US national trust bank charter takes effect Judge questions CFTC authority but doesn’t halt trading Following the CMAA’s complaint, US District Judge Valerie Caproni said the plaintiff was likely to succeed in its claim that the CFTC exceeded its statutory authority by allowing stock perps to trade as security futures. Caproni found that the contracts appeared to qualify as swaps rather than security futures, casting doubt on the agency’s legal interpretation. However, she denied CMAA’s request for a temporary restraining order, finding that the group had failed to demonstrate imminent, irreparable harm. The decision left the CFTC’s trading approvals in place while the lawsuit proceeds. CMAA is scheduled to file its reply to the CFTC’s opposition to a preliminary injunction on Tuesday. Magazine: What Democrats’ US midterm sweep means for the CLARITY Act

items.titleTr: Binance warns iOS flaw could expose crypto wallet keys
items.summaryTr: The exchange urged iPhone users to remove apps installed from untrusted sources, and it is unclear whether Apple’s latest iOS updates fix the flaw.
items.articleText: Binance warns iOS flaw could expose crypto wallet keys The exchange urged iPhone users to remove apps installed from untrusted sources, and it is unclear whether Apple’s latest iOS updates fix the flaw. Update (Nov. 10, 2026, 12:14 pm UTC): This article has been updated to include a response from a Binance spokesperson. Cryptocurrency exchange Binance warned Tuesday that an iOS flaw could expose crypto wallet recovery phrases and private keys if a user runs a malicious app on an affected iPhone. Binance listed iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1 and 27.2 among the affected versions that could allow malicious apps to read local files from other apps, putting seed phrases, private keys and login credentials “at risk across the entire ecosystem.” Binance added that this was “an iOS-level issue, not unique to Binance.” Binance urged users to delete any apps installed from untrusted sources, update iOS and all apps to the latest official versions, and transfer funds to new wallets created on clean devices if they suspect a breach already occurred. Blockchain security firm SlowMist flagged the issue earlier on Tuesday, saying a malicious app could read recovery phrases if a wallet stores them unencrypted on the device. An iOS security researcher who goes by forcequitOS publicly disclosed the flaw on Sunday and credited another researcher who goes by 0xjohnny. Apple released iOS 27.2.1 and 26.7.3 on Monday, but it remains unclear whether either update fixes the flaw. Cointelegraph contacted Apple about the vulnerability, but had not received a response by publication. A spokesperson for Binance told Cointelegraph that the “underlying file-access risk may apply across the iOS ecosystem” but said it identified no confirmed cases where attackers used this bug to access cryptocurrency wallets or steal funds. Related: Binance hackers move 81% of stolen Solana, route funds via THORChain

items.title: Ex-employee sues Ethereum Foundation and Vitalik Buterin over firing
items.summary: Kayleen Fulton alleges she was fired less than two weeks after disclosing a cancer diagnosis and helping organize a staff letter challenging a requirement to endorse the foundation’s new mandate.

items.titleTr: Ex-employee sues Ethereum Foundation and Vitalik Buterin over firing
items.summaryTr: Kayleen Fulton alleges she was fired less than two weeks after disclosing a cancer diagnosis and helping organize a staff letter challenging a requirement to endorse the foundation’s new mandate.
items.articleText: Ex-employee sues Ethereum Foundation and Vitalik Buterin over firing Kayleen Fulton alleges she was fired less than two weeks after disclosing a cancer diagnosis and helping organize a staff letter challenging a requirement to endorse the foundation’s new mandate. A former Ethereum Foundation employee has sued the organization, along with Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin and four others. Kayleen Fulton alleges she was fired after disclosing a cancer diagnosis and organizing a staff letter challenging a directive tied to the foundation’s new mandate. Fulton, who led the foundation’s protocol support team and is known in the Ethereum community as “Nixo,” filed the complaint on Nov. 4 in the United States District Court for the District of Colorado. She alleges that Bastian Aue, a co-executive director at the time, fired her on April 6, 13 days after she disclosed her diagnosis. The complaint also alleges Buterin helped adopt and enforce the directive as a board member. Fulton said she and colleague Trent Van Epps organized a letter in response to the mandate with 53 signers. It backed the mandate’s goals while objecting to a requirement that employees affirm it to keep their jobs. The complaint alleges that days later, on April 6, Aue fired Fulton and Van Epps 30 minutes apart. Fulton alleges disability discrimination, retaliation and interference with her medical leave rights and is seeking lost pay and damages. The complaint also says some employees objected to a reference to ritual suicide in the mandate and quotes Aue as telling staff that the language was figurative. In a May 14 letter quoted in the complaint, a lawyer for the foundation’s Singapore affiliate, Ethereum Asia Pacific Limited, denied that Fulton had been subjected to unlawful conduct or retaliation and said her separation agreement was binding. Cointelegraph reached out to the foundation, Fulton and Van Epps for comment, but had not received a response by publication. The foundation published its mandate in March, charting out its role in Ethereum’s ongoing and future development. It highlighted censorship resistance, open-source code, privacy and security, and said it would focus on protocol upgrades, research and developer tools. Magazine: Vitalik ‘pivots’ ETH to store of value, crypto suffers after US midterms: Hodler’s Digest

items.title: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
items.articleText: Release Number 9324-26 CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers November 09, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced eight orders filing and settling charges against Michael Talento, Anthony Tyler Williams, Quillan Roberto Black, Christopher Williams, Michael Levi Peters, Jordan Taylor Morgan, Lewis Matthew Neal, and Tyler Evan MacKechnie for acting as unregistered associated persons of unregistered foreign introducing brokers. According to the orders, the introducing brokers engaged in the solicitation of orders for off-exchange leveraged or margined retail foreign currency and retail commodities transactions with U.S. customers who were not eligible contract participants. The respondents solicited those customers without registering as associated persons of the introducing brokers, as required. Under the orders, the respondents must cease and desist from engaging in their illegal conduct. They also are barred for two years from registering with the Commission in any capacity or acting as a principal, agent, or employee of any CFTC registrant. Each order also recognizes the penalty the respondent owes in a related Securities and Exchange Commission proceeding. These orders relate to a prior Commission order sanctioning Netrios LP Ltd. and Red Acre Ltd. for facilitating illegal off-exchange commodity transactions with U.S. customers. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9263-26] The SEC has filed and settled charges against the respondents based on the same underlying conduct. The CFTC thanks the SEC for its assistance. -CFTC-

According to the orders, the introducing brokers engaged in the solicitation of orders for off-exchange leveraged or margined retail foreign currency and retail commodities transactions with U.S. customers who were not eligible contract participants. The respondents solicited those customers without registering as associated persons of the introducing brokers, as required. Under the orders, the respondents must cease and desist from engaging in their illegal conduct. They also are barred for two years from registering with the Commission in any capacity or acting as a principal, agent, or employee of any CFTC registrant. Each order also recognizes the penalty the respondent owes in a related Securities and Exchange Commission proceeding. These orders relate to a prior Commission order sanctioning Netrios LP Ltd. and Red Acre Ltd. for facilitating illegal off-exchange commodity transactions with U.S. customers. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9263-26] The SEC has filed and settled charges against the respondents based on the same underlying conduct. The CFTC thanks the SEC for its assistance. -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
items.articleText: Release Number 9323-26 CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today issued an interpretation (“Interpretation”) of the requirement that designated contract markets (“DCMs”) provide competitive, open, fair, and impartial access to their members and persons with trading privileges under Commission Regulation 38.151(b) (“Impartial Access Requirements”). “Derivatives markets must operate on a uniform basis at a national scale in order to achieve the purposes set out in the Commodity Exchange Act,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Geographic access restrictions are inconsistent with those purposes and the Act’s impartial access requirements.” DCMs must cease domestic geographic restrictions that violate the Impartial Access Requirements within 30 days, or else submit to the Division of Market Oversight (“Division”) an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. Further, within 30 days, DCMs should ensure that intermediaries accessing their markets are not impeding and are complying with the DCM’s Impartial Access Requirements, or else submit to the Division an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. The Commission will consider the facts and circumstances of any particular case in connection with potential Commission action. -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
items.articleText: Release Number 9321-26 CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets November 04, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to safeguard the integrity of U.S. agricultural markets. The MOU will allow the CFTC and USDA to harmonize policies and practices to better share information and increase access to risk management tools. The agreement will also assist both agencies with monitoring and identifying structural or potential systematic risks, among other things. “For decades, America’s agricultural community has relied on our markets to hedge risk, manage uncertainty, and plan for the future,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I’m proud that the CFTC and USDA have formalized this partnership through an MOU that will strengthen protections for America’s farmers, ranchers, and producers while expanding opportunities to manage risk through more efficient data sharing. I commend Secretary Rollins for her partnership and commitment to a more coordinated regulatory approach that safeguards the integrity of our markets and ensures they continue serving the agricultural community that feeds and clothes our nation.” “Faster and more transparent data sharing between USDA and CFTC is critical to helping our farmers and ranchers navigate an ever-changing market,” said USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This MOU builds upon USDA’s ongoing data modernization efforts and allows our agencies to collaboratively identify risks and improve responses to market events. Breaking down barriers between government agencies to deliver for our customers is a hallmark of this administration and I am looking forward to the successes this MOU will bring.” -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
items.articleText: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
items.articleText: Release Number 9319-26 CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig today released a statement announcing that perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities can begin trading for the first time on designated contract markets that are dually registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as notice-registered national securities exchanges to trade security futures products. Key excerpts from Chairman Selig’s statement: “Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the ‘Equity Perps’) can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges. … “This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures that have led to their emergence as widely sought tools for risk-management and price-discovery. I believe that bringing these types of innovative products into our regulated markets ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues. … “The Equity Perps build on the foundation of the [Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000] and the [CFTC-SEC Memorandum of Understanding]. For too long, regulatory uncertainty left innovative products, such as security futures and equity perpetual futures, stranded in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins has aptly described as a regulatory ‘no man’s land’ due to a lack of harmonization between the agencies. The CFTC and SEC have turned the page on that era, and are committed to delivering regulatory clarity for innovative products and a clear path to market, rather than more casualties of jurisdictional disputes.” Read Chairman Selig’s full statement here. -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
items.articleText: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. Market structure evolves best through thoughtful and responsible progress, and that’s exactly why we’re hosting a roundtable to hear directly from industry on their views for 24/7 trading across different asset classes,” Chairman Selig said. The roundtable will take place at CFTC’s headquarters in Washington. Information regarding the agenda, speakers, and registration will be posted at a later date. This event will be open to the public and livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Please note the number of in-person participants may be limited, and visitors will be subject to security checks. Members of the public are welcome to submit speaker nominations to [email protected]. -CFTC-

items.title: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
items.articleText: Release Number 9317-26 ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026 October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — Last week, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Risk Management Center at Kansas State University co-hosted the 2026 Agricultural Commodity Futures Conference (AgCon) in Overland Park, Kansas. The two-day conference brought together industry leaders, policymakers, and market participants to examine critical issues facing the agricultural economy, developments in derivatives markets, and the risk management tools American farmers, ranchers, and agribusinesses depend on. Conference Highlights CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig joined K-State President Richard Linton to welcome participants on opening day. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig addressed conference attendees, “I have spent a lot of time this year traveling around the country and talking to farmers and ranchers working hard each day to provide the food, feed, and fiber we depend on throughout our country and the world. I’ve met with farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and energy producers in Iowa, Texas, Nebraska, South Carolina, and Florida, and now, I’m with all of you here in Kansas.” [Watch Chairman Selig’s full remarks here.] Following Chairman Selig’s remarks, panelists examined the relationship between cash and derivatives markets, evolving commodity contracts, and the importance of effective hedging tools for agricultural producers. There were also panels where industry representatives addressed access to agricultural credit and the financial challenges facing producers and merchants. Additional afternoon discussions focused on rising production costs, fluctuating commodity prices, supply chain disruptions, and broader pressures on the farm economy. In addition, conference participants engaged in discussions about emerging market developments, including perpetual futures, 24/7 trading, and tokenized collateral, and their implications for agricultural risk management. CFTC Chief Advisor Alex Titus and White House Council of Economic Advisers Member Aaron Hedlund also examined the U.S. economic outlook, agricultural trade, and policies shaping American agriculture. The first day concluded with a keynote address from U.S. Department of Agriculture Deputy Secretary Stephen Vaden. U.S. Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas opened the second day with a morning keynote address on agricultural policy and legislative priorities facing American producers. The morning continued with discussions on agricultural prediction markets, the use of data in modern commodity markets, and developments in event contracts. In addition, panelists examined superintelligence, information advantages, and market integrity, including the implications of emerging technologies for market participants and regulators. Chairman Selig joined Futures Industry Association President and CEO Walt Lukken for a fireside chat examining the Commission’s priorities, the evolving regulatory landscape, and developments shaping derivatives markets. The conference concluded with discussions on enhancing public understanding of markets through data and customer education, followed by a panel examining clearing, market access, and the role of intermediaries in derivatives markets. Chairman Selig delivered closing remarks, concluding AgCon2026. -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
items.articleText: Release Number 9316-26 CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig announced the CFTC’s plan to increase the publication frequency of the Commitments of Traders Report (COT Report) from once to twice a week by the end of 2026. Data from Monday will be published on Wednesday, and data from Wednesday will be published on Friday. Both reports will be released at 3:30 p.m. ET on their respective publication days. Under the enhanced publication schedule, the reports’ latency will decrease from three days to two days. The change follows the Commission’s recent Request for Comment and reflects its commitment to providing market participants with more timely information about trading positions and activity in agricultural markets. The CFTC’s Division of Data is leading the effort to operationalize the expanded publication schedule through modernization and automation while maintaining accuracy. “COT Reports have been an important source of transparency for decades. Following feedback from the agricultural community, I’m pleased to announce the CFTC will be rolling out COT Reports twice a week to ensure this information stream is as useful as possible,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. -CFTC-
